review.speaker_notes: The preacher is an older male teaching pastor at Fellowship Bible Church (FBC) Tucson. He is never introduced by name inside the sermon, but the service host closes at [01:27:02] with 'So I think we can wrap up I think by saying that Pat painted a picture that the world out there is very different...' — so 'Pat'. Self-references: 'my mother gave me a name when I was four years old and called me the world king' [00:45:59]; 'the longer I preach, the longer I live, it's not about becoming smarter or brighter' [01:05:06 area, 00:51:06]; 'I calculated the sermons I'm going to preach that by 2028 we should be finished' [00:51:51]; 'that's the pastor coaching me' [00:55:47]. He is highly interactive with the room: he names individuals present (Josh [01:04:01], Rocco [01:06:22], Dave [01:14:26], Ginger [01:12:36]), runs call-and-response ('say deep conviction... say it louder' [00:55:28]), tells the congregation to stand up and shout, and jokes 'We need to become a black church... we need some enthusiasm' [01:06:43]. Audience is a small congregation with a visible older cohort ('several older ones of us losing our spouses, caring for our spouses who are not able to care for themselves' [01:13:45]). This is week 2 of a series in 1 Thessalonians ('last Sunday I asked you to consider prioritizing the reading of the Apostle Paul's letter' [00:34:20]).

outline_fbc: Recap of last week's two assignments: read 1 Thessalonians a chapter a day, and write someone a letter containing nothing but appreciation, love and joy (0:34:14)
Public reading of 1 Thessalonians 1:1-7 and opening prayer (0:35:37)
'News you can use': George Barna's American Worldview Inventory 2026 — the eight worldview categories, only 4% of American adults hold a biblical worldview, only 4% read the Bible daily (0:36:53)

Why Paul wrote a letter: culture then and now; the letter is 'not facts and figures but the heart of a pastor pouring out his great joy for those in whom he's been the spiritual OBGYN'; the 'sandwich technique' of affirmation-meat-affirmation (0:42:10)

Verse 1a — the writers: 'Paul' means little/small; Chrysostom's 'man three cubits tall'; the Acts of Paul and Thecla physical description; Ephesians 3:8; small in his own estimation, large in his understanding of God; Isaiah 66:2 (0:43:48)
Rembrandt's portrait of Paul — putting a face to a real man with a real team (0:47:28)
Silas/Sylvanus, god of the woods, Pennsylvania, the jail duet in Philippi; Timothy, Acts 16:1, 'Timid Tim', 'imitate me as I imitate Jesus', surrender over trying harder (0:48:10)

Verse 1b — the recipients: 'ekklesia' in Athens, in the Septuagint, in 1 Peter 2:9; 'we're not just talking about a group of people who on Sundays go into a building... there were no buildings'; verse 4, 'brothers and sisters loved by God' (0:52:14)

Verse 1c — the greeting: grace and peace as the two indispensable 'growth catalyzers'; ancient vs modern letter openings; Acts 9 and Saul the persecutor; grace the fountain, peace the stream; the peace the junkie/the porn-addicted long for; Strait of Hormuz and hope not in government (0:56:56)
First cause for thankfulness: 'the work which springs from faith' — faith and works, a warm living faith that issues in action, being 'broken' like a stallion, the acrostic JOY (1:03:41)

Second cause: 'labor prompted by love' — the trivialized 'labor of love' (mowing the lawn, a cup of coffee) vs kopos-style sweat and fatigue; Spurgeon 'they came to watch me burn'; agape and 'Love so amazing, so divine'; passion as prerequisite — 'unless we learn to love like this, we will never labor like this' (1:06:31)

Third cause: 'endurance inspired by hope' — not passive resignation but active constancy; Ginger's car and CarShield; the aging congregation; John Harbaugh's firing and 'attack the day with an enthusiasm unknown to mankind' (1:11:45)
Application to FBC: 'we want them to see a faith that functions, a love that labors, and a hope that endures'; closing prayer (1:16:49)
outline_begg: Every local church will be known for something; the church at Thessalonica was known throughout the world
Suggestion: read 1 Thessalonians every day for the next month (five chapters, about 79 verses)
Historical background: Acts 16 — the Macedonian vision, obedience turning Christianity westward; Philippi, the beating, the jail, the midnight singing
Acts 17 — Thessalonica, the Via Egnatia, the three-week synagogue crusade, the God-fearing Greeks, the riot; Berea, Athens, Corinth
Paul at Corinth 'in weakness and fear and much trembling'; no theology for suffering in the modern church; the Spirit moves him on by opposition

Timothy's good news from Thessalonica (1 Thess 3:6) is what prompts the letter; aside — 'write somebody a letter which contains nothing other than an expression of your concern for them and your joy in them'

Verse 1: 'Paul' means little (as does 'Begg'); Chrysostom's man three cubits tall; the Acts of Paul and Thecla description; least of all the saints (Eph 3:8); small in his estimation, large in his understanding of God; the humble and contrite man (Isa 66:2)
His colleagues: Silas/Sylvanus, god of the woods, Sylvan, Pennsylvania, William Penn, the 50% of the duet in the Philippian jail; Timothy the timid man

The recipients: ekklesia in Athens, in the Septuagint, in 1 Peter 2:9; 'not just... a group of people who went into a building, for there was no building into which to go'; verse 4 'whom God had chosen', verse 5 'not simply with words but with power'; Father and Son, plus the Spirit — the triune God building his church

The greeting: grace and peace; Acts 9 and Saul of Tarsus the persecutor now on the receiving end of the beatings; 'grace is the fountain and peace is the stream which issues from it'; John 14 peace; the materialist's ladder and the junkie's high
Three causes of thankfulness: (1) the work which springs from faith — faith not works, but good works characterize the life of faith

(2) the labor prompted by love — the trivialized 'labor of love' (mowing the lawn, a cup of tea), kopos as sweat, fatigue, weariness; agape, the love that cost God his Son; 'Love so amazing, so divine, demands something'; the shrug is the answer and the answer is no; 'until we learn to love like this, we'll never labor like this'
(3) the endurance inspired by hope — not quiet passive resignation but active constancy in the face of extreme difficulty; William Barclay and George Matheson's prayer
Application to Parkside: 'a faith that functions... a love that labors... a hope that hangs on'; closing prayer
review.outline_comparison: Same skeleton, minus Begg's long Acts 16-18 travelogue. From the moment the FBC preacher reaches 'here we move into chapter 1, verse one' [00:43:48] to the final 'Amen' [01:18:35], the sequence of ideas is Begg's, point for point and in Begg's order: Paul-means-little (Chrysostom, Thecla, Eph 3:8, Isa 66:2) -> Silas/Sylvanus/Pennsylvania and Timothy -> ekklesia and 'no buildings' -> Father and Son plus the Spirit -> grace and peace, Saul of Tarsus, fountain-and-stream, the junkie -> the three causes of thankfulness in Begg's headings ('the work which springs from faith', 'the labor prompted by love', 'the endurance inspired by hope') -> the closing triad 'a faith that functions, a love that labors, a hope that endures/hangs on' -> a closing prayer that follows Begg's prayer clause by clause. The FBC preacher drops Begg's 25-minute Acts background section and substitutes a Barna worldview-survey opener, and he inserts his own illustrations at Begg's illustration slots. Where Begg's structure changes, the FBC sermon changes with it.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher replaces Begg's entire 25-minute Acts 16-18 historical background with a contemporary-research opener, and he substitutes his own illustrations at most of Begg's illustration slots while keeping Begg's exegetical skeleton, headings, phrasing and closing prayer. The original content is almost entirely (a) the Barna worldview-survey introduction, (b) sports/pop-culture illustrations, (c) local and personal references, and (d) heavy call-and-response interaction with the room. Almost none of the original material is exegetical: where the sermon explains the text, it is Begg's explanation.
examples: The whole 'news that you can use' opener on Dr. George Barna's American Worldview Inventory 2026 — the eight categories, 'only 4% of American adults possess a solid biblical worldview', the Family Feud bit ('out of a 100 adults, how many of them read the Bible daily?') (0:36:53-0:42:10)
The 'sandwich technique' for helping someone grow — affirmation, then the meat/admonition, then 'you're loved by God, you're loved by me' (0:43:01)

Personal story: 'my mother gave me a name when I was four years old and called me the world king. I I've really never struggled with feeling good about myself because of a mom' (0:45:59), reprised at 1:10:05
Rembrandt's 16th-century portrait of Paul projected on screen, and the jab 'Teenagers don't know what that is because they spend much of their time with the headsets on' (0:47:28-0:48:02)

The expanded Timothy material: Acts 16:1, 'two different value systems', 'Timid Tim', 'take a little wine for your stomach, for your ulcers', 'Imitate me as I imitate Jesus... it's false humility to say oh don't follow me' (0:48:52-0:51:00)

The playground-picking illustration: 'when you lined up at the park to pick sides... there's always that person who's last... That was never me until I got into college' and 'You're the pick of the litter' (0:54:16-0:54:43)
Sustained congregational call-and-response drilling verse 5 — 'say deep conviction... Say it louder... Stand up' and 'I think the 4% just became 5%' (0:54:53-0:56:00)
'Bless their heart... which really means they're dumb as a rock' and heaping burning coals (1:00:56); the pornography addition alongside Begg's junkie (1:01:40)
Current events: the Strait of Hormuz closure and 'if you think our hope is in government... you're in trouble' (1:02:35-1:03:10)
The broken-stallion definition of brokenness ('we're not talking about your bones breaking... a wild stallion that has been broken in') and the JOY acrostic (1:05:07-1:05:38)
Spurgeon's 'they came to watch me burn' (1:08:03), the kamikaze pilot with 131 missions (1:09:15), and the chicken-and-pig-breakfast joke with the self-aware 'That's supposed to be funnier' (1:09:23)
'Most churches live for the ABCs, attendance, buildings, and cash' (1:09:54)

Local: Ginger's car and CarShield — 'I think the name should be car stall... who was helping? The church' (1:12:36-1:13:16); naming Josh, Rocco and Dave in the room; the congregation's aging members caring for spouses (1:13:45)

The extended John Harbaugh illustration: fired over the phone by Steve Biscotti, consoling the owner, Jack Harbaugh's 'attack the day with enthusiasm that is unknown to mankind', and hired by the Giants — 'I'm putting my money on the giants' (1:14:45-1:16:44)

personalisation_patterns: British details Americanised: Begg's 'I bring my wife a cup of tea in the morning' becomes 'I brought my spouse a cup of coffee in the morning' (1:07:17).
Begg's own church name swapped for the local one: 'they may think of Parkside Church' becomes 'When others think of you and us as a church... when they think of the people at FBC' (1:16:56).
Begg's unnamed authority kept unnamed but warmed up: 'One of the commentators says' becomes 'I I love this comment. A commentator said this very helpfully' (1:00:41).

Begg's self-deprecating aside about his own surname ('the name Begg means little... a Gallic name') is dropped and replaced with the preacher's own name story: 'my mother gave me a name when I was four years old and called me the world king' (0:45:59).

Begg's declarative sentences converted into call-and-response for a participatory room: 'for there was no building into which to go' becomes 'You know why? There were no buildings' (0:53:17); 'he who is humble and contrite in spirit' becomes 'Let's say that together' (0:46:48).

Begg's dated cultural markers refreshed: Begg's materialist climbing a ladder propped against the wrong wall is dropped for pornography addiction; Begg's 'late 20th century' Cleveland framing is replaced by 2026 Barna data and the Strait of Hormuz.

Begg's illustration slots preserved but refilled: at the 'labor/burning' slot Begg's 'burned out for the cause of Jesus Christ' triggers a Spurgeon quotation of the FBC preacher's own; at the endurance slot Begg's Barclay/George Matheson quotation is replaced by the Harbaugh family story.

Superlatives added to Begg's restrained phrasing: 'a love that cost God his son' becomes 'the love that costs God his only son'; 'we're rightly jealous of this church' becomes 'how proper it is to be rightly envious of this church'.
review.rating_rationale: From verse 1 onward this sermon is Begg's sermon on the same text, re-delivered: the exegetical points, their order, their headings, and most of the connective prose track 'Faith, Hope and Love' clause by clause, and the machine alignment finds 23 overlapping regions covering roughly 18% of the sermon window even before accounting for looser paraphrase. The borrowings are of the strongest kind — an unattributed commentator quote, an apocryphal description of Paul, a four-step etymological digression about Pennsylvania, two paired 'labor of love' vignettes, the 'shrug is the answer' peroration, the closing 'faith that functions / love that labors / hope that endures' tagline, and finally a closing prayer prayed back almost clause for clause. Begg is never named, Truth For Life is never named, and no borrowing is signalled in any form; the preacher instead tells the congregation this is material 'that I never heard before I studied it'. It is not a 10 because the delivery is genuinely his own: he discards Begg's entire Acts background section, opens with 2026 Barna research, adds a dozen original illustrations (Harbaugh, Spurgeon, CarShield, the sandwich technique, the world-king story), and reworks the whole thing into a call-and-response style utterly unlike Begg's. But the sermon's spine, its scholarship and its prayer are borrowed wholesale.

FBC [1:17:30]: 'Oh Lord, how proper it is to be rightly envious of this church... we want to be prepared to labor to the point of weariness, fatigue, and perspiration... we want not to face a Monday with grim resignation, but active constancy.' | BEGG: 'Oh, Lord, we're rightly jealous of this church... We want, Lord, to be prepared to labor to the point of wearingness, fatigue, and perspiration... And we want, Lord, not to face a Monday with grim resignation, but with active constancy.'
caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captions and the Begg text is Whisper ASR; both mangle proper nouns identically in places (Chrysostom -> 'Christom'/'Chrysostom', Thecla -> 'Thela'/'Fechler', Sylvanus -> 'Sylvanius'/'Sovenas'), so exact-word identity scores understate the real overlap and occasional odd wording ('his Roman improper name', 'a second century doctrine') is likely a transcription error rather than the preacher's.

Alignment regions 1, 2, 3, 8 and 14 are Scripture (1 Thess 1:1-5, Isaiah 66:2, John 14:27) being read or quoted by both men and are NOT evidence of borrowing; region 5 is flagged 'likely_scripture Ezekiel' by the heuristic but is actually the apocryphal Acts of Paul and Thecla description, which IS strong evidence.

Some overlapping phrases are stock evangelical or standard reference-work material and carry little weight on their own: 'grace and peace', the ekklesia/Athens-assembly gloss, 1 Peter 2:9 'out of darkness into his marvelous light', the Watts hymn line 'Love so amazing, so divine', and 'salvation is by faith not works'. The evidence here rests on the sequence and the connective prose around them, not on any single phrase.

The FBC preacher's two congregational assignments (read the letter daily; write someone a letter of appreciation) were given the previous Sunday and are only recapped in this recording, so the borrowing of Begg's two asides is attested here at second hand.

I checked the other 21 Begg transcripts in source_transcripts/ for the FBC-original illustrations (Spurgeon 'watch me burn', Harbaugh, Barna, the sandwich technique, kamikaze pilot, Rembrandt, 'pick of the litter', 'attendance, buildings and cash') and found no matches, so this sermon draws on volume1/01-faithhopelove and no other Begg message in the archive.
Timestamps are caption cue starts and can lag the spoken word by a second or two.

review.speaker_notes: The preacher is the long-tenured senior pastor of Fellowship Bible Church, Tucson. He is never named in this transcript, but he is identified as 'Pastor Pat' in the sibling sermons in this playlist (e.g. Your_True_Identity_-_071226 at 0:08:34 'Thank you, Pastor Pat'; Sexual_Purity_-_062826 at 1:02:05 'it's the pastor Pat paraphrase'), and in this sermon he quotes his wife addressing him by that name at 1:07:43 ('right, Pat, do you want to get married?'). Self-references: 'having been able to live for 40 years of being a pastor' (1:11:21); 'if you've been through the battles like I have for 40 years' (1:14:05); 'I haven't had those types of issues uh with this church in the last 35 years as I did at the start' (1:17:45); 'Cindy and I have been married for close to 40 years' (1:15:06); he is wearing a cast and recovering from a leg injury (0:15:12) and refers to having 'cut my hand nearly off' (1:16:00). Audience cues: Mother's Day 2026 service, Mother's Day banquet after the service, prime rib, blood drive, 'Discover FBC' membership class; he addresses 'church', asks for hands from moms, jokes with worship leader Karen and Kevin, says 'Thank you, Roco' (1:12:55) after a laugh line. He also speaks to the congregation directly about himself as their pastor ('You should feel free to assess the ministry of anyone including myself or this church', 1:08:30).

outline_fbc: Introduction: this is not a Mother's Day message, but 1 Thessalonians gives the most touching glimpse into Paul's heart; Romans reveals his mind, 1 Thessalonians reveals his heart (0:51:10)

Historical background from Acts 17: three Sabbaths in the synagogue, some persuaded, then jealousy, a mob, a riot, and a night-time escape to Berea - the church 'in the maternity ward' one day after birth (0:51:53-0:53:53)
Paul's later travels, Timothy's report, and the slanderous accusations behind chapter 2: 'he ran away, didn't he?' (0:53:53-0:56:34)

Point 1 (vv. 1-2): an honest assessment of his visit - suffering and outrage in Philippi (Acts 16), yet 'with the help of our God we dared to tell you the gospel'; people only suffer for what they truly believe; the repeated 'you know' shows the facts were common knowledge (0:57:05-1:01:12)

Point 2 (vv. 3-4): his present appeal - the commentator's catalogue of cults and cranks; our message is true, our methodology above board, our motives pure; how to spot the con men; dokimazo and 2 Timothy 2:15 (1:01:14-1:06:13)
Point 3 (vv. 5-6): his past approach - no flattery (kolakia), no mask over greed, no hunger for praise; personal story of vowing candour with Cindy (1:06:13-1:08:24)

Application: assess any ministry by the man, the message and the motives; the pastor is responsible not to the church or its boards but to God; why he would never pastor a congregational voting church (1:08:24-1:11:11)
Jonathan Edwards: dismissed by congregational vote in July 1750, only 10% voting to keep him; David Hall's eyewitness account; 1 Corinthians 4:3-5 (1:11:11-1:15:06)

Personal testimony: Cindy's father Lt. Col. Joseph Morrison, wanting to hear 'well done'; the near-loss of his hand; pastors tyrannised by the roller coaster of adulation and criticism; no seminary and no church can make a pastor - only God, through suffering (1:15:06-1:18:35)
Close on vv. 6-8: 'like a nursing mother' - wanting to pastor FBC as long as God allows, a community that sees his flaws and loves him; a rule for candid speech; closing prayer (1:18:35-1:21:22)
outline_begg: Chapters 2-3 give the most touching glimpse into the heart of Paul; Romans reveals his mind, 1 Thessalonians reveals his heart
Historical context from Acts 17: the synagogue, three Sabbaths, some persuaded, jealousy, bad characters from the marketplace, a riot, and the humiliating night departure to Berea

The opponents used his hasty disappearance to call his ministry into question; without the slanderous accusations chapter 2 makes no sense; he answers out of concern for two things - the truth of the gospel and the future of the church

First (vv. 1-2): an honest assessment of the details of their visit - the Philippian jail of Acts 16; people only suffer for what they believe; 'we dared to tell you' means outspokenness, frankness, plainness of speech; the repeated 'you know' shows the facts were common knowledge; John Stott on leaders with nothing to hide; contemporary clergy scandals

Secondly (vv. 3-4): his present appeal - Phillips' paraphrase; the pastor is a steward not an owner; the commentator's catalogue of cults, crackpots and cranks; three things - our message is true, our methods above board, our motives pure; how to identify the con men; dokimazo and 2 Timothy 2:15
Thirdly (vv. 5-6): his past approach - no flattery (kolakia), no mask to veil greed, no hungering for compliments
Test of ministry: the man, his message and his motives; the minister is primarily responsible neither to the church nor to its boards but to God himself - disconcerting yet freeing

Jonathan Edwards thrown out of his church; 1 Corinthians 4:3-5; pastors tyrannised by the roller coaster of adulation and criticism; no seminary and no church can make a pastor, only God; verses 7ff give an amazing model for ministry; closing prayer
review.outline_comparison: Same skeleton, in the same order, down to the sub-points. Both open with the identical 'Romans reveals the mind / 1 Thessalonians reveals the heart' framing, both then detour to Acts 17 for the birth of the church, both reconstruct the same imagined slander ('he ran away, didn't he?'), both then walk the identical three-part division (vv. 1-2 honest assessment of the visit / vv. 3-4 present appeal / vv. 5-6 past approach, flagged by the change of tense), both pause at the same word studies (dokimazo with 2 Timothy 2:15; kolakia as a New Testament hapax), both apply it with the same triad 'the man, the message, the motives', both land on the pastor being responsible to God rather than to the church or its boards, and both illustrate with Jonathan Edwards followed by 1 Corinthians 4:3-5 and the 'roller coaster' of adulation and criticism, closing with 'no seminary can ever make a pastor... only God can do that.' The FBC preacher inserts his own stories and a Mother's Day frame, and he continues a little past Begg's stopping point into vv. 7-8, but he does not depart from Begg's sequence anywhere in between.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher adds a Mother's Day frame at the front and back, a substantial expansion of the Jonathan Edwards illustration, several long personal stories from his own marriage and ministry, and contemporary American application. None of Begg's structure is displaced by this - the original material is inserted between Begg's points rather than replacing them. The biggest genuinely independent stretches are (a) the Mother's Day framing and the 'maternity ward' image for the newborn Thessalonian church, (b) his own family stories, (c) the Edwards research (Whitefield, the July 1750 vote, the 10% figure, the David Hall eyewitness quotation) which goes well beyond Begg's one-sentence mention, and (d) the closing section on vv. 7-8, which Begg does not reach in this message. He also drops Begg's John Stott quotations, Begg's Philippians-paraphrase reading, Begg's Irish clergy-scandal news item, and Begg's Mary Baker Eddy / Book of Mormon / Hindu avatars list, substituting American equivalents.

personalisation_patterns: Begg's 'Let me quote from one commentator' becomes 'I like to quote from one commentator where he says this' - a one-off act of citation turned into a stated personal habit (1:01:47).

Begg's 'So, for example, you take the ministry of Jonathan Edwards' becomes 'So for example, I love this illustration. It's the ministry of Jonathan Edwards' - the borrowed illustration is claimed as a personal favourite (1:11:40).

Begg's 'This was written before the late 20th century. We might be able to rival it now' becomes 'Now again, this commentator is writing uh before the late 20th century. You know what? I think that our culture might be able to rival that' - the borrowed aside is reframed as a fresh personal observation (1:01:59).
Begg's 'so many pastors live tyrannized in that dilemma' becomes 'so many pastors I know live tyrannized' - eyewitness authority added to a borrowed sentence (1:17:00).

Begg's impersonal 'the stewards of the gospel... are primarily responsible neither to the church nor to its boards' becomes a signposted personal conviction: 'I'm going to say something strong and then I'm going to defend it. Paul is saying that the pastor is not primarily responsible neither to the church nor to its boards but to God himself' (1:09:44).

Begg's generic 'it is really freeing to be in this situation' becomes 'having been able to live for 40 years of being a pastor, it is really freeing to be in this situation' - forty years of experience attached to a borrowed line (1:11:21).

Begg's evening-service markers are converted to Sunday morning: 'the verses before us this evening' becomes 'the verses that are before us here' (0:56:19); Begg's 'I want to say to you tonight' disappears.

Begg's British/Irish references are Americanised: the Irish Catholic clergy scandal becomes the internet and conspiracy theories; 'they gave you a hiding' becomes 'they gave you a beating'; 'bishops or synods' is dropped; the 'Aegean highway' becomes 'the Ignatian highway' with an American revivalist image ('like a love brother love and his traveling salvation show').
Begg's third-person 'he says' for Paul is regularly converted to the name: 'Paul is saying', 'and here's what Paul says. It's right there in the text.'

Begg's congregation-specific probes ('Is that what you get when you worship in this place? ... your Sunday school teacher ... your youth group') are compressed into one FBC-specific invitation: 'You should feel free to assess the ministry of anyone including myself or this church' (1:08:30).

Begg's cited authorities are dropped while his anonymous ones are kept: John Stott is quoted twice by Begg and never by FBC, but the unnamed commentator - the one quotation with no attributable source - is the one that survives.
review.rating_rationale: This message follows Begg's 'No Clever Tricks' from its first sentence to its final peroration without ever leaving his sequence: the same opening antithesis, the same Acts 17 detour, the same reconstructed slander, the same three-part division marked by the same change of tense, the same two Greek word studies with the same cross-references, the same anonymous commentator quotation with the same framing aside, the same 'man, message, motives' test, the same Jonathan Edwards illustration followed by the same 1 Corinthians 4 passage, and the same closing 'no seminary... no church... only God' triad. Dozens of non-Scripture phrases are verbatim or near-verbatim ('the evangelist and his sidekick', 'unless disengaged of their senses', 'the hard edge of discipleship', 'primarily responsible neither to the church nor to its boards', 'ecclesiastical committee', 'the roller coaster of emotion', 'live tyrannized'), and the machine alignment understates this because it misses whole borrowed paragraphs such as the 'speaking freely, speaking openly, speaking fearlessly' word study. Begg is never named, and the one citation cue in the sermon ('I like to quote from one commentator') is itself lifted from Begg. It is not a 10 because roughly a third of the delivery is genuinely the FBC preacher's own - the Mother's Day frame, a researched expansion of the Edwards story, several substantial personal stories, and a closing section on vv. 7-8 that Begg never reaches - and because he re-orders and compresses in places rather than reading a manuscript.

caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captions of a live service and contains obvious ASR errors: 'phrasiology' for 'phraseology', 'adgulation' for 'adulation', 'publicly fgged' for 'publicly flogged', 'disciplehip' for 'discipleship', 'George Witzfield' for 'George Whitefield', 'humiliation departure' for 'humiliating departure', 'dokamazo'/'Dakamazo' for 'dokimazo', 'A kolakia' for 'kolakia'. Quoted excerpts are verbatim from the captions, so some words are certainly mis-transcribed; the argument rests on the sequence and on multi-word constructions, not on single words.

The Begg source is likewise a Whisper transcript with its own errors - 'John Stark' for John Stott, 'Philippine' for Philippi, 'publicly flawed' for flogged, 'the stalks' for the stocks, 'role-coaster' for roller coaster, 'docha madzuil' for dokimazo, 'started our riot' for 'started a riot'. Where the two transcripts differ slightly, ASR noise is often the explanation rather than genuine rewording.

Scripture read or quoted by both men is not evidence of borrowing. Alignment regions 1-4, 7, 22 and 28 are simply 1 Thessalonians 2:3-5 and 1 Corinthians 4:3-5 in a modern translation, and regions 6, 8, 14 and 18 mix a verse with commentary. These have been classified as scripture/mixed and carry no weight in the rating; the case rests entirely on the non-Scripture regions.

Some overlapping language is genuine evangelical stock ('stewards of the gospel', 'curry favor', 'the truth of the gospel', 'above board') and would be weak evidence on its own. It is only the density, ordering and the presence of idiosyncratic constructions alongside it that make the case.

The alignment file's coverage figure (35.8% of the sermon window) is a floor, not a ceiling: several clearly dependent passages - notably the 'speaking freely, speaking openly, speaking fearlessly' word study at 1:00:03 and the 'kolakia' discussion at 1:06:38 - fall below the fuzzy-match threshold and are not flagged as regions.

The FBC preacher is not identified by name in this transcript; the identification as 'Pastor Pat' comes from other sermons in the same playlist and from his wife's reported speech at 1:07:43. No claim is made here about the FBC preacher's intent - only about the textual relationship between the two messages.

Grepping distinctive phrases across all of source_transcripts/ (volumes 1-3) turned up no material from any other Begg sermon in this message; the dependence is on volume1/04-noclevertricks alone. source_consumption.title: The Word of God, Not Men

review.speaker_notes: Preached by the senior pastor of Fellowship Bible Church (Tucson). He is never introduced by name in the captions, but he names himself in an aside at 1:18:22: "when I'm in heaven, God one day will look at me and said, 'I got one thing against you, Pat.'" — i.e. Pat. He refers to his wife Cindy (1:19:38, 1:14:15 area), his daughter "Caitlyn"/"Kayla" (1:14:02), his old football coach Jim Young (1:17:48), staff member Karen Giggstat (1:04:21) and "Pastor Brian" (1:14:54). A second, different voice (a co-host/associate) runs the announcements and graduate recognition earlier in the service and says "My granddaughter Kendra Bird" (0:50:16); that man is NOT the preacher. Audience cues are heavily local and congregational: Memorial Day weekend, two graduates (Ryder Campbell, Kendra Bird), NextGen kids' classes, the 9:00 a.m. prayer group in the pastor's office, Kellen Elementary teacher breakfast, the Amazon/Peru church-planting video, Kenya, "church center" app, "many, many churches in this city". Interjections and call-and-response ("Amen", "How many of you can say amen...") mark a Sunday-morning contemporary service.
review.boundary_note: The graduate-recognition segment and its prayer end at 0:57:30. At [00:57:31.760] the preacher pivots: "Okay. Well, hey, let's go ahead and open our Bibles to this section before us. It's first Thessalonians chapter 2. I'm going to read verse 13 and 14. And then we'll we'll preach." I take that as the start (scripture reading + the opening prayer at 0:58:33 are included per the brief). He reads 1 Thess 2:13-16, prays, and the exposition proper begins at [00:59:04] "Now, the last time we saw Paul's humane heart...". The closing prayer runs from [01:30:16] "Lord, please. I guess personally I forgive me..." and ends "Amen." at [01:31:14.400]; music/"How Great Thou Art" begins at [01:31:25.688]. So the sermon window is 0:57:33-1:31:14 (~33.5 minutes).

attribution.notes: No signal of any kind that the sermon's skeleton, its exegetical moves, its commentator quotation, its application questions or its closing prayer come from another preacher. The preacher does flag borrowed material when the source is one HE chose: "I want to illustrate that by telling kind of an anecdote called the night the power went out. It's written by a lady who's the power in their house goes out" (1:08:51); "like Pastor Eve Hill used to say" (1:24:10); "what my football coach Jim Young used to tell us in practice" (1:17:48); "a story that Karen Giggstat was telling us, sharing with the staff this week" (1:04:19). The contrast is telling: he cites the incidental illustrations but not the sermon itself. The one place he cites a book source, Leon Morris, he presents as his own reading ("has a very helpful thought in this uh of his observations") — Begg's own sentence is "Leon Morris has a very helpful comment on this as he addresses this in his commentary." He also presents the four-P outline as his own: "Now, with that as an intro, I've got four points to make that begin with the letter P" (1:01:11), against Begg's "Now, I have a number of points this evening, all that begin with the [letter] P."

outline_fbc: Intro: last time we saw Paul's pastoral heart — father, mother, and now herald; 'truth that is not softened by love can become dreadfully hard and love that is not hardened by truth can become dreadfully soft' (0:59:04)
'I've got four points to make that begin with the letter P' (1:01:11)
1. The PROCESS — 'from us / of God / at work in you'; a study in prepositions; Leon Morris quote; Isaiah 66:2 humility and trembling (1:01:15)

1a. Two requisites: a praying congregation (1:06:09) — Spurgeon's furnace room, 'the night the power went out', BC ('before church') time, prayer for missions/America — and a believing congregation (1:07:12)
2. The PRODUCT — 'you became imitators of God's churches in Judea'; three application questions about what our church would give others to imitate (1:19:21)
2a. Product also = suffering; Acts 17 background, Jewish opposition, Paul turning to the Gentiles (1:22:15)

3. The PERSECUTION — v.14b 'you suffered from your own countrymen'; Pharisees and Sadducees, 'first century cancel culture'; Paul's truth balanced by love (Philippians 'rubbish', Romans 3:1-2, Romans 9:2-3) (1:24:42)

4. The PROCLAMATION — was it antisemitism? No: 'not a racial prejudice... a theological conviction'; past or future tense (famine 45-47 / destruction of Jerusalem); closing challenge: 'Would you rather shake in fear or would you begin to tremble at the truth of God's word' (1:29:46)
Closing prayer (1:30:16-1:31:14)
outline_begg: Intro: last time, Paul's pastoral metaphors — father, mother, herald (kerusso, v.9); 'truth that is not softened by love can become dreadfully hard and love that is not hardened by truth can become dreadfully soft'
'Now, I have a number of points this evening, all that begin with the [letter] P'

1. The PROCESS — from us / of God / in you; 'He's really a study in prepositions'; Leon Morris commentary quote and its application; two foundations: an expectant praying congregation, and preachers convinced they hold the word of God; 'there are many, many churches where this process never takes place'

2. The PRODUCT — James: be doers not hearers; 'you became imitators of God's churches in Judea'; the ski-school illustration; 'if people came from other churches to imitate Parkside Church, what would we give them to imitate?'; product also = suffering (Acts 17 background, Jewish opposition, turning to the Gentiles)
3. The PERSECUTION — a five-fold list: they killed the Lord Jesus (with Matthew 27:24-25), killed the prophets (Matthew 23:29), drove us out, displeased God, are hostile to all men

4. The PRONOUNCEMENT — v.16 'heaping up their sins to the limit'; God's patience running out (Amos); past/present/future tense: famine of AD 45-47, massacre of AD 49, or destruction of Jerusalem AD 70; Paul was fiercely Jewish (Philippians 'rubbish', Gamaliel, Romans 3:1-2, Romans 9:2-5)

Conclusion: a survey of the church's own guilt in anti-Judaism (Chrysostom, Lateran Council 1215, the Crusades, Luther's 'The Jews and Their Lies', Bonhoeffer, slavery); 'the best of men are men at best'; it was anti-Judaism, 'a theological conviction... not a racial prejudice'
Closing prayer
review.outline_comparison: Same skeleton. Both sermons run on an identical alliterated four-point frame announced the same way — Begg: 'I have a number of points this evening, all that begin with the [letter] P'; FBC: 'I've got four points to make that begin with the letter P' — and the first three headings are word-for-word the same (Process, Product, Persecution) in the same order, arriving in the same sequence of sub-moves (prepositions -> Leon Morris -> praying congregation -> 'many, many churches' -> James, doers not hearers -> imitators of Judea -> 'what would they find as the distinctive hallmarks of our church family' -> Acts 17 pursuit narrative -> Paul was fiercely Jewish -> Philippians 'rubbish'/Gamaliel -> Romans 3:1 -> Romans 9:2 -> famine of 45-47 / destruction of Jerusalem -> closing prayer). Only the fourth P differs in name: Begg's PRONOUNCEMENT (God's wrath) becomes FBC's PROCLAMATION (a call to tremble). The differences are additive rather than structural: the FBC preacher hugely expands Begg's two-sentence 'praying congregation' point into roughly thirteen minutes of his own local material, and he drops Begg's ski illustration, Begg's five-fold list of Jewish sins, and Begg's long church-history survey — while still keeping Begg's punchline from that survey ('a theological conviction... not a racial prejudice') and Begg's closing prayer.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher's substantial original contribution is concentrated in one place: Begg devotes two sentences to 'the absolute necessity of an expectant praying congregation', and the FBC preacher expands that into roughly thirteen minutes (1:05:46-1:19:20) of wholly independent material — a NextGen classroom anecdote, a Spurgeon 'furnace room' illustration interleaved with a 'the night the power went out' story, a week-by-week prayer plan mapped onto the church's own ministries, missions video narration, 2 Chronicles 7:14 applied to America, and family/coach anecdotes. He also adds an Isaiah 66:2 'shake vs. tremble' motif that becomes the sermon's through-line and its closing challenge, renames Begg's fourth point 'proclamation' instead of 'pronouncement', and drops Begg's ski illustration, his five-fold list of the sins of Paul's opponents, and his long church-history survey (Chrysostom, Lateran Council 1215, the Crusades, Luther, Bonhoeffer). Local colour throughout is his own: Memorial Day weekend, the graduates, Fellowship Bible Church's ministries, Tucson. Everything that is exegetical or structural, however, is Begg's.

review.rating_rationale: The sermon's entire architecture is Begg's: the announced four-point alliterated outline, the first three headings in the same order, and within them the same sequence of exegetical moves — herald/kerusso at 2:9, the from-us/of-God/in-you 'study in prepositions', the Leon Morris quotation with Morris's second sentence and Begg's connective, the 'many, many churches' complaint, James on hearers and doers, the imagined delegation to Judea, the 'what would they find as the distinctive hallmarks of our church family' application with its four-item list, the Acts 17 pursuit narrative, 'Paul was fiercely Jewish', mom-and-dad-and-Gamaliel, Romans 3:1-2, Romans 9:2-3, Amos and the tipping scales, the famine-of-45-47 versus destruction-of-Jerusalem option set, and finally the closing prayer, which is Begg's almost word for word. None of this is attributed, and the quotation that IS attributed (Morris) is presented as the preacher's own reading. What holds the rating below 9-10 is genuine reworking: he never simply reads Begg aloud, most passages are reworded, and about 45% of the running time — chiefly a thirteen-minute expansion of Begg's two-sentence 'praying congregation' point, plus local illustrations, the Isaiah 66:2 trembling motif and a renamed fourth point — is his own. But the dependence is not incidental; strip the local illustrations out and what remains is Begg's sermon in the preacher's own voice.
report_quotes: FBC (1:20:52): "If people came from other churches to find out what we're doing and what we're all about, what would we model for them to imitate as a church? What would they find was distinctive hallmarks of our church family?" | BEGG: "if people came from other churches to imitate Parkside Church, what would we give them to imitate?... What would they find as the kind of distinctive hallmarks of our church family?"

FBC (1:26:38): "So is he saying that his mom and dad taught him rubbish? Is he saying that his training under Gileiel had been garbage?" | BEGG: "he didn't mean that his mom and dad had taught him rubbish and he didn't mean that his training under Gamaliel had been rubbish"

FBC (1:30:33, closing prayer): "so much confusion abounds in our schools and universities and the thorough affairs of our lives. And it's hard to engage people. In fact, the task is so daunting it drives us to our knees." | BEGG (closing prayer): "so much confusion abounds in our schools and universities in the thoroughfares of our lives it's hard to engage people in fact the task is so daunting it drives us to our knees"
caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captioning of a live service and the Begg text is Whisper ASR of a cassette-era recording; both contain mishearings ('coruso'/'Kyrusol' for kerusso, 'Gileiel'/'Gamaliel', 'Eve Hill' for E. V. Hill, 'thorough affairs' for 'thoroughfares', 'Berea'/'Burya'). Word-level identity figures should therefore be read as floors, not exact measures.

Alignment regions 1-6 and 19 are both preachers reading the same Bible passages (1 Thess 2:13-16; Romans 9:2-3) and are NOT evidence of borrowing. Region 5-6's 'Revelation 15' label and region 15's 'likely_scripture Philippians 4' label are false positives from the scripture detector: region 5-6 is 1 Thess 2:16, and region 15 ('how to be united, how to be expectant, how to be rejoicing, how to be progressing') is Begg's own composition, not Scripture.

The two preachers use different English versions (FBC reads NIV 2011 — 'not as a human word', 'brothers and sisters', 'your own people'; Begg reads NIV 1984 — 'not as the word of men', 'brothers', 'your own countrymen'), so the shared wording in the reading passages is version overlap, not copying. Notably, when the FBC preacher EXPOUNDS rather than reads, he reverts to Begg's older wording: 'you accepted it not as the word of men' (1:00:54).

Some shared items are evangelical stock and carry little weight on their own: 'be doers of the word, not hearers only', 'the word of God at work in you', prayer-meeting-as-powerhouse language, and the general truth-and-love framing.

The FBC sermon shows no detectable dependence on any of the other 21 Begg sermons in source_transcripts/ — greps for its distinctive non-Begg material (Spurgeon's furnace room, 'clean the fish', 'afflicts the comfortable', 'tribulating', 'cancel culture', 'vitamin A', the 2% rule) return nothing across the corpus, and the only near-match outside 06-thewordofgodnotmen is the truth/love aphorism, which Begg himself first delivered in 05-truthandlove and back-references in 06. The Isaiah 66:2 'humble and contrite... trembles at his word' allusion appears in passing in volume1/01-faithhopelove, but the FBC preacher's sustained use of it is structurally unlike Begg's and is best treated as independent.
Timestamps are caption start-times and can lag the spoken word by a second or two.
The preacher's name 'Pat' is inferred from a single self-referential aside (1:18:24); he is never formally introduced in the captioned portion.

review.speaker_notes: The preacher is the senior pastor of Fellowship Bible Church, Tucson, named 'Pat' (self-reference at 1:05:56: 'Some people say, "Pat, why don't you give more invitations here for people to come and walk the aisle?"'). He is almost certainly the 'Patrick' in the childhood sibling photo he puts on screen at 0:44:21 ('my oldest sister Beverly there, my brother Mike, my sister Kathy, and off there in the distance ... is is is Patrick there, staring off into space'). Wife is Cindy (0:56:20); three grown children, two now back in Tucson with grandchildren and the oldest in California (0:57:26). Spent years in Little Rock and has been back in Tucson 37 years (0:54:13). Former athletic coach (1:06:56: 'I would always tell athletes as a coach'). Friend of Roger Blumenthal, pastor of Pantano Christian Church (0:49:51). He is NOT the man who does the announcements and membership covenant earlier (that speaker says 'Thanks, Pat' at 0:09:50). Audience cues: small congregation where he 'know[s] everybody's name' (0:50:12), heavy call-and-response ('Say that with me', 'Say amen if you got them', 'Say this, I'm chosen by God', 'turn to the person next to you to say, "Hi, brother. Hi, sister"'), on-screen slides for the Greek word, Tucson/Arizona heat references, new-member recognition, Father's Day barbecue.

outline_fbc: Setting: 'Team Thessalonica' - Paul, Silas and Timothy had enemies who charged insincere motives and abandonment; Paul answers from 2:17 into ch. 3 (0:41:11)
Frame: the image of a nurturing parent; 'you're like a son to me' expresses the deepest affection possible (0:42:26)
Announced three points: 'the source, the force and the course' of genuine affection (0:43:06)

I. THE SOURCE - the key word 'brothers and sisters' (v.17); 2 Thess 2:13-15, Rom 8:28-30, Eph 2:12-13; affection is not superficial but substantial; 'flat is the ground at the foot of the cross'; adoption / 'you're family' (0:44:02)

II. THE FORCE - two forces: (a) Paul's own longing, never away in thought; the Greek 'orphan' word; personal empty-nest illustration; (b) Satan blocking the way, with the Stott quotation, and God overruling all evil for good - 'This is not Star Wars theology' (0:53:13)
III. THE COURSE - v.19-20 looks forward into heaven; hope, joy, crown; Phil 2:16, Phil 4:1, 1 Cor 9:2, 1 Cor 9:19 (1:01:26)
Application: tomorrow morning, look for divine appointments; be the only Bible someone reads; ask God for just one person (1:05:20)
Recap of source / force / course and closing prayer (1:06:27)
outline_begg: Setting: Paul, Silas and Timothy had enemies suggesting malevolence and abandonment, that their spiritual parents 'had been too frightened to come back'; Paul rebuts from v.17 into ch. 3
Frame: the pattern of his pastoral care is the best of parental care; John Stott and Chrysostom quoted on Paul's affection
Announced three points: 'note with me the source, the force, and the course of this affection'

I. THE SOURCE - the key word 'brothers'; 2 Thess 2:13-15, Rom 8:28-30, Ephesians; not superficial but substantial; 'the ground is flat at the foot of the cross'; 'we're all adopted children tonight'; communion-table application and the hymn 'Not what I have gotten... only a sinner saved by grace'

II. THE FORCE - never away in thought; 'there is never a day in eleven and a half years'; the Greek word 'aporphanisthentes'/orphan; the honeymoon-departure / father-in-law's movie camera illustration; Satan stopped us, the commentaries, the Stott quotation, God overrules all evil for good
III. THE COURSE - v.19-20 looks forward into heaven; hope, joy, crown; Phil 2, Phil 4:1, 1 Cor 9; the Galatians 'boast only in the cross' objection answered

Application: tomorrow morning, your objective is to see unbelieving people become committed followers; word to mothers; Chrysostom's 'not even light itself'; Samuel Rutherford / Anne Ross Cousin's 'if one soul from Anwoth meets me at God's right hand'
Recap of source / force / course and closing prayer before communion
review.outline_comparison: Same skeleton, same sequence, and largely the same sentences. The FBC sermon follows Begg's three-point alliteration ('the source, the force and the course'), his order of supporting texts (2 Thess 2:13-15, Rom 8:28-30, Eph 2, then Phil 2:16, Phil 4:1, 1 Cor 9), his sub-moves (the 'brothers' key word, 'not superficial but substantial', 'the ground is flat at the foot of the cross', the Greek 'orphan' word, the commentaries aside, the Stott quotation, the athlete's crown, the 'tomorrow morning, loved ones' charge) and even his closing recap verbatim. The differences are subtractions and substitutions rather than a different design: FBC drops Begg's communion setting, the Chrysostom quotations, the hymn, the Rutherford/Anne Ross Cousin poem and the Galatians objection, and drops in his own illustrations (family photo, Little Rock, empty-nest 'booster rocket syndrome', Pantano Christian Church, the Babadog prayer). Nothing in the FBC outline is structurally independent of Begg.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher supplies his own delivery layer: a stand-up opening, congregational call-and-response, on-screen family photo, and a full set of substitute illustrations. Every one of Begg's set-piece illustrations and quotations is dropped (Chrysostom twice, John Stott's 'he felt and acted towards them as if they were his own children', the hymn 'only a sinner saved by grace', the honeymoon departure on a Russian ship and the father-in-law's shaking movie camera, the Samuel Rutherford / Anne Ross Cousin 'Anwoth' poem, the word to mothers, the Galatians 'boast only in the cross' objection, and the whole communion-table setting) and replaced with Tucson material. He also adds a small amount of his own exegetical decoration (the two-force framing of point II, the rearview-mirror image, Ephesians 2:12 read out). What he does not add is any independent argument: the interpretive spine, the sequence of texts, and the transitions are all Begg's.

personalisation_patterns: Begg's secondhand citation becomes the FBC preacher's own reading: 'again I found John Stott to be so helpful' -> 'I found John Stodd, a great theologian, so helpful' (0:59:38), with no mention of where he met the quotation.
Begg's observation becomes a claim of personal study: 'to notice this little driving phrase in Paul's life' -> 'It took me a while to dig up this phrase in Paul's life' (1:05:04).

Begg's autobiography is re-based on the preacher's own: 'never a day in eleven and a half years... my father my sisters' (Begg on Scotland) -> 'in this dream called Little Rock, that's 37 years passed now... not a day that passed that I did not think of my father, uh my mother, my brother, my sisters' (0:54:13).

Begg's parental-separation illustration (leaving New York on a Russian ship; the father-in-law weeping behind the movie camera) is swapped for a same-slot, same-purpose FBC illustration (empty nest, 'booster rocket syndrome') while the surrounding sentences stay Begg's (0:55:55-0:58:10).

Communion language is patched out because there is no communion: 'those whom we welcome with regularity around this table' -> 'someone you talk with with regularity' (1:07:57); Begg's 'the wonder of the hymn that we have just sung' -> 'at the cross' (0:51:23); 'We're all adopted children tonight' -> 'How many of us have been adopted by God? Look around the room' (0:52:08).
Begg's dated list item is modernised: 'the issues of substance and financial provision or its absence' -> 'the matters of the right and the left of politics' (0:50:58).

Statements become congregational call-and-response: Begg's 'the source, the force, and the course' -> 'We're going to consider the source. Say that with me' (0:43:08); Begg's 'these individuals had been chosen by God, that they had been called to faith through the preaching of the gospel' -> 'Say this, I'm chosen by God... Say, the gospel has been preached to me' (0:46:42).

Aphorisms are lightly re-ordered rather than rewritten: 'the ground is flat at the foot of the cross' -> 'flat is the ground at the foot of the cross' (0:50:42); 'quickening and renewing and changing' -> 'quickening, renewing, charging you' (1:06:39).

Begg's third-person narration of Paul is converted to direct address and repetition: 'missing them dreadfully, profoundly anxious on their account' -> 'I'm missing you dreadfully. I'm profoundly anxious of your account' (0:58:10).
review.rating_rationale: This sermon is Begg's 'Our Glory and Joy' re-preached. The FBC message takes Begg's alliterated outline (source / force / course), his opening prayer, his sequence of supporting texts, his exegesis of the Greek 'orphan' word, his aside about the commentaries, his one named authority (John Stott) with Begg's own words of introduction, his imagined objector, his hinge sentences between points, his athlete's-crown line, his closing charge and his entire three-question peroration - often at 0.8-0.96 token identity across stretches of 25 to 150 words that are not Scripture. The machine alignment finds 33 regions covering roughly a third of the sermon window, and the borrowings are not clustered in the Bible reading: the strongest matches (Regions 10, 15, 25, 28, 30, 32) are Begg's own prose. It is not a 10 because the preacher does not read Begg's manuscript straight through: he drops every one of Begg's illustrations and quotations except Stott, substitutes his own Tucson stories, adds a heavy layer of congregational interaction, and writes his own closing prayer. But the sermon's argument, its order, and a large share of its actual sentences are Begg's, delivered without any attribution.
report_quotes: FBC (0:40:36): 'So take this small section from this letter. May it fill our hearts, instruct our minds, and by the Holy Spirit transform our lives. For we do look to you and you alone in Christ's name. Amen.' | BEGG: 'Father, we pray that this brief section from this letter may instruct our minds and fill our hearts and change our lives. Only you can do this, and so together we look to you in Jesus' name. Amen.'

FBC (0:59:37): 'I found John Stodd, a great theologian, so helpful because here's what he says about this. Since we lack this information, it's better for us to confess our ignorance than to express an unwarranted confidence.' | BEGG: 'again I found John Stott to be so helpful... he said since we lack this information it is better for us to confess our ignorance than to express an unwarranted confidence.'

FBC (1:06:27): 'So what's the source of this genuine affection?... Nothing other than the very blood of Christ. What's the force of such affection? It's the power of the Holy Spirit quickening, renewing... What's the course of this affection? It's a course that began in eternity, walks through time, and looks forward to the day that we will be gathered around God's throne.' | BEGG: 'what is the source of this genuine affection? It is found in the very blood of the Lord Jesus Christ. What is the force of such affection? It is the power of the Holy Spirit quickening and renewing and changing. What is the course of this affection? It is a course that began in eternity, walks through time, and looks forward to the day when we will be gathered around God's throne.'
caveats: Both transcripts are ASR. The FBC text is YouTube auto-captions (no [music] tags, no speaker names beyond '>>', occasional all-caps runs and mishearings such as 'John Stodd' for John Stott, 'forneew' for foreknew, 'exaltations' for exultation, 'genuiness' for genuineness, 'Babadog' for a Tucson peak). The Begg text is Whisper ASR and contains its own errors ('I pauled it again and again' for 'I, Paul, did', 'John Stark' for John Stott, 'a porphanetsomai' for aporphanisthentes, 'possesates' for a word that is probably 'pulsates', 'Ross Cousin' for Anne Ross Cousin). Small wording differences between the two may therefore be transcription noise rather than real divergence - which if anything understates the identity.

The reading of 1 Thessalonians 2:17-20 (Regions 2, 3, 4, 16, 17, 27) and the quotations of 2 Thessalonians 2:13-15, Romans 8:28-30, Ephesians 2:12-13, Philippians 2:16, Philippians 4:1 and 1 Corinthians 9:19 are Scripture in a shared translation (NIV 1984) and are NOT by themselves evidence of borrowing. What is evidentially significant is that the same texts appear in the same order with the same introductory framing.
Several shared phrases are evangelical stock ('the blood of Christ', 'the family of God', 'the body of Christ', 'brothers and sisters in Christ') and carry little weight on their own.

Alignment scripture labels are unreliable in places - e.g. Region 5 is tagged '2 Chronicles 36', Region 18 'Matthew 18', Regions 17 and 21 'Jeremiah 44' - and these are false positives; the underlying text in each case is Begg's prose, which is why they are classified as non_scripture or mixed here.

No borrowing from any other Begg sermon in source_transcripts/ was found: greps for the FBC sermon's distinctive non-Begg material ('Star Wars', 'smelling salts', 'booster', 'opera lady', 'rearview', 'attitude of gratitude', 'icing on the cake', 'shield of faith', 'divine appointments', 'three-foot circle', 'Pantano') return nothing across volumes 1-3. The dependence appears to be on this one paired sermon.

Begg preached this at an evening communion service; FBC is a Sunday morning service with no communion, so a handful of borrowed lines had to be re-tailored. Those seams are part of the evidence, not a sign of independence.
Timestamps are caption start times and can lag or lead the spoken word by a second or two.

review.speaker_notes: The preacher is 'Pat' — the worship leader prays at 0:38:07 'that you would anoint Pat to bring the message of purity to our hearts', and at 1:02:05 he calls his own rendering of 1 Thess 4:4 'the pastor Pat paraphrase'. Heavy autobiography identifies him further: wife Cindy (married 45 years, three kids, four grandkids), son Matthew born ~Dec 1981, daughter Caitlyn who turned 16 in 2006; he was a youth pastor who did Dallas Theological Seminary's Masters of Biblical Studies over two summers in the mid-1980s. Local Tucson cues: Bear Canyon Library, 'Tankerie [Tanque Verde] to Wentworth', Park Place Mall, Center for Arizona Policy voter guides, Fellowship Bible Church. Audience is a full intergenerational service ('the whole assembly of ages'), and he repeatedly frames the message as training for parents and grandparents ('I'm creating a NGC, next generation equipping course'). He explicitly says this continues last week's message on pleasing God ('here we are back to this big picture that we started last week').
review.boundary_note: The worship leader's prayer ends at 0:38:26 ('the church said, Amen'). Pat begins speaking at 0:38:28 ('It's so exciting to be here and worshiping the Lord'), moves into his framing remarks about talking about sex, prays at 0:39:15, reads 1 Thessalonians 4:1-8 at 0:39:52-0:41:01, and preaches. He closes reading 1 Thess 4:9-10 at 1:15:39 and prays from 1:16:55, ending 'Amen' at 1:18:03; the band's 'Speak, O Lord' starts at 1:18:22. Announcements before (0:12:21-0:17:20) and the second closing prayer plus 'let's do lunch' announcement after 1:27:10 are excluded.
review.passage: 1 Thessalonians 4:1-8 (with 4:9-10 read at the close; also cites 1 Thess 3:13 and 5:23)

attribution.notes: Alistair Begg and Truth For Life are never named, and the sermon is never presented as anyone else's outline. The named sources are exactly the ones Begg also names in these two sermons, and in two cases they are the very quotations Begg uses. At 1:03:57: 'CS Lewis had the best expression on this. He says, "If you really want to know what the intentions of a guy are and you're going to have sex, find out what they do five minutes after the act is over." And then he says, "After the cigarettes are all smoked, rarely does one keep the rapper."' — Begg (Part Two): 'C.S. Lewis puts it as graphically as any. When he says if you want to know how much interest a man has ... watch him five minutes afterwards and then he says no one keeps the packet when they've smoked the cigarettes.' At 1:13:58: 'what I love about this is JB Phillips ... he paraphrases it and he makes clear one word' — Begg: 'Philips paraphrases it, make a clean cut with all sexual immorality.' Two borrowed items are stripped of their attribution entirely: Begg quotes the commentator I. H. Marshall by name — 'Marshall puts it in this way where things are evil, the Christian attitude is necessarily one of abstention and not of moderation' — and at 1:15:13 the FBC preacher delivers it as his own summary: 'when things are evil, the Christian attitude is not to be one of moderation, but it's to be abstinence.' Likewise Begg's 'it's said by some' framing survives at 0:53:40 ('It's said by some that the conditions in which Paul lived in century 1 are very different from our own') without any hint that the answering argument is also borrowed. The one genuinely signposted source is his own: 'In 1982, Cindy and I were at a conference ... marriage counselor Norm Wright posed a question' (0:41:01).

outline_fbc: Opening personal story: Norm Wright's 1982 question — the mark of genuine Christianity in the 21st century will be 'they will stay married'; Pat's own near-drift during a Dallas seminary summer; 'high fidelity' wordplay (0:41:01)

The big picture / bird's-eye view: seeing the valley of your life from the mountain; Jesus 'I always do what pleases him' (John 8), 2 Cor 5:9, Eph 5:10; pleasing God is not personal preference but a divine imperative — 'God does not exist to serve us, we exist to serve him' (0:45:49)
The world's counter-message: the cosmos/anti-Christ thought system, 'sexual clutter', the devil dressing poison in seductive attire, no fidelity marketed as high fidelity (0:48:55)
Why this teaching still has authority, and why it is for every age — 'training for you to teach your kids ... a next generation equipping course' (0:50:12)
Historical setting: Corinth, the temple of Aphrodite, 'what happens in Corinth stays in Corinth'; Thessalonica no better (0:53:34)
Verse 3 — 'It is God's will that you should be sanctified'; set up the teaching as a question-and-answer dialogue between the 'earth child' and heaven-bound Paul (0:55:34)
First responsibility (v.4): learn to control your own body impulses — illustrated by Caitlyn's 1983 Honda Accord, the punctured gas tank and the $300 in cash; 'the pastor Pat paraphrase' (0:56:49)
Application: when is a teenager ready to date? Self-government first; counsel to girls and boys; C.S. Lewis on the cigarette packet; 50-80 year old men not yet ready to date (1:03:23)
Second and third responsibilities (vv.5-6): not in passionate lust; defrauding another is 'not a bullet ... it's a bomb' (1:05:44)

The dialogue continues: 'surely he won't mind if I occasionally mess up' → the Lord will punish (v.6b); 'you're over the top' → v.7 holiness; 'we don't break God's laws, God's laws break us'; v.8 — rejecting this rejects God (1:06:29)
The Holy Spirit as power source; 1 Thess 3:13 and 5:23 — 'the one who calls you is faithful and he will do it'; the teenager's '11 more years' objection (1:09:42)
How sanctification happens: the scriptures in daily devotion (Ps 119:9, cited as 'Proverbs 19:9'); saints are ordinary people; the marriage 'list went to history' illustration (1:11:45)
The concrete example: 'avoid sexual immorality' — J.B. Phillips' 'clean cut'; the mangled creature on the road; the tonsils; abstinence not moderation (1:13:41)
Close: reading 1 Thess 4:9-10; live holy for wife and children; thrive in Babylon, public schools, 'you will go out as a missile'; closing prayer (1:15:25)
outline_begg: Part One: 'Finally, brothers, we instructed you how to live in order to please God' — Jesus (John 8) 'I always do what pleases him', Paul (2 Cor 5) 'we make it our aim to please him', Ephesians 5:10 'find out what pleases the Lord'
Part One: pleasing God is not personal preference but a divine imperative — 'God does not exist for us, but we exist for him ... we exist in order that we might live to the praise of his glory'

Part One: Paul is not penning his own peculiar prescriptions — 'this is not the preoccupations of the Apostle Paul, this is the word of God himself'; pleasing God is the foundation of all our ethical Christian behavior
Part One: the three areas of chapter 4 — sex, work, death; 'there are no more prominent notions in many of our minds'

review.outline_comparison: Partly the same skeleton, and the shared part is the expository spine. The FBC sermon opens and closes with material that is entirely its own (Norm Wright, the seminary-summer story, the Honda Accord, Babylon/public schools), but the moment it turns to the text at 0:46:54 it follows Begg's Part One almost step for step: the same three proof texts in the same order (John 8, 2 Cor 5, Eph 5:10), the same thesis sentence about aspirations and the praise of his glory, the same 'do we have the right to be so bold and forceful' objection, the same Corinth/Aphrodite/Thessalonica background answering the same rhetorical question, the same reading of vv.3-8 as an imaginary dialogue with the same sequence of objections, the same 3:13→5:23 encouragement with the same '11 years / no girlfriend' teenager, and the same closing run of sanctification-by-scripture → marriage list → Phillips 'clean cut' → mangled creature → tonsils → abstinence not moderation. Part Two is used far less but is not untouched: the C.S. Lewis cigarette quote, the poison-in-beautiful-wrapping image, the single/divorced/widowed question and the Pharisee warning all come from it. What FBC adds is not a different structure but interpolated personal illustration inside Begg's frame, plus one genuinely independent device (the bird's-eye view/valley picture) carried over from his own previous week.

original_material.summary: Roughly half the sermon by clock time is the FBC preacher's own, and it is genuinely his: two long autobiographical narratives, a controlling visual metaphor he brought from his own previous week, a distinctive pedagogical frame (equipping parents and grandparents to have this conversation), and a set of blunt local applications about dating that have no counterpart in Begg. He is also a different kind of preacher — anecdotal, Americanised, politically engaged — where Begg is expository and doctrinal. What he does not supply is the exposition: every time he leaves a story and returns to the text, he returns to Begg's sequence, Begg's illustrations and often Begg's sentences. Notably absent from the FBC version are Begg's crisis-process-crisis doctrine of sanctification, the drill sergeant illustration, Elisabeth Elliot's '60 seconds a minute', the Romans 5/6/8 chain, John Stott's two statements and his testimony on singleness, and the Romans 1 material — so the borrowing is selective, not a wholesale reading of the manuscript.

personalisation_patterns: Begg's neutral 'the individual' in the imaginary dialogue becomes a named character with a folksy label — 'the earth child' talking to heaven-bound Paul — which makes an adopted device look like an invented one.

Begg's 'I've been helped by viewing this paragraph here as one half of a conversation' becomes 'Imagine yourself as the teacher of a conversation ... you'll start seeing vision for your life and your ministry': the reader's aid Begg offers is re-pitched as the audience's own ministry tool.

Borrowed illustrations are introduced with markers of personal disclosure: the marriage-list illustration arrives as 'I think you'll get it. And I'll share this' (1:12:46), and Marshall's sentence arrives as 'So, let's put it this way' (1:15:13).

British details are Americanised inside otherwise verbatim borrowings: 'cinema' becomes 'movie' (and gains 'you text'); Begg's 'wee bit over the top' becomes 'reading it over the top'; Begg's 'man' in 1 Thess 4:8 becomes the NIV's 'a human being'.

Attribution is unevenly preserved: J.B. Phillips and C.S. Lewis (whom Begg names) are named; I. H. Marshall (whom Begg also names) is dropped and his sentence absorbed; Begg himself is never named at any point.

Begg's background material is compressed and then topped with a local joke — the Aphrodite/Corinth paragraph is reproduced closely and then capped with 'a lot like Vegas ... what happens in Corenth stays in Corenth'.

Where Begg gives a doctrinal excursus (crisis-process-crisis, Romans 5-8, the drill sergeant), FBC substitutes a family anecdote of comparable length (the Honda Accord), so the borrowed spine is padded out with original narrative rather than original exegesis.
Traces of reading rather than handling the text: 'verse five of chapter 23' for 1 Thess 5:23, and 'Proverbs 19:9' for Psalm 119:9 — both points where Begg's spoken source gives no clean citation.
review.rating_rationale: This sermon is not more independent than the others in the series once you look past the personal material — the machine's 6.5% coverage badly understates it, because most of the reuse is compressed paraphrase rather than verbatim strings. Every element of the exposition is Begg's: the opening trio of proof texts in his order, his thesis sentence about aspirations and the praise of his glory reproduced word for word, his 'bold and forceful' objection, his Corinth/Aphrodite background answering his rhetorical question, his imaginary dialogue as the sermon's entire organising device with its objections in his sequence, his 3:13→5:23 encouragement, his eleven-years teenager, his marriage-list illustration, his Phillips 'clean cut', his roadkill and his tonsils, and Marshall's line with the attribution removed. Part Two is used less but is demonstrably in hand: the C.S. Lewis cigarette quote with its superlative framing, the poison-in-beautiful-wrapping image, the single/divorced/widowed question and the closing Pharisee warning. What holds the rating at 7 rather than higher is that roughly half the running time is authentically the preacher's own — the Norm Wright frame, the near-miss on the flight to Dallas, the bird's-eye-view metaphor from his own previous week, the Honda Accord, the dating counsel — and that he leaves out large tracts of Begg (the crisis-process-crisis doctrine, the drill sergeant, Elisabeth Elliot, Stott, Romans 1). The result is a genuinely personal sermon built on a borrowed and unacknowledged expository skeleton.

Exact wording should be checked against audio before publication, though the overlaps here are far too long and too specific to be transcription artefacts.

Both men are preaching 1 Thessalonians 4:1-8 from the NIV, so shared Scripture wording is expected and proves nothing. Alignment Regions 1, 2, 8 and 10 are essentially the biblical text and are excluded from the case; Regions 7, 11, 12 and 13 are the biblical text wrapped in Begg's own connective phrasing, and only the wrapper counts as evidence.

Some shared items are genuinely common property in conservative evangelical preaching and are treated as weak evidence: the Corinth/Aphrodite background (standard commentary material, though the wording here is not), warnings about the Pharisee spirit, 'we don't break God's laws, God's laws break us', and the general claim that the first century was as immoral as our own.

The C.S. Lewis and J.B. Phillips quotations circulate widely and could in principle have been picked up elsewhere; what makes them evidential is that they appear alongside Begg's framing language, in Begg's order, inside passages that are otherwise near-verbatim.

outline_fbc: Cold open: have you ever tried to decode Revelation to find the date? 'today is the day you will find out that no one knows' (0:43:11)

Reading of all eleven verses before the verse-by-verse (0:48:01)

But here's the thing is I could be wrong' (1:06:29-1:11:17)
