outline_begg: VOLUME2/08 'The Coming of the Lord, Part Two' (1 Thess 5:1-8). Long prologue on views of history: Lily Tomlin's bag lady Trudy and 'I worry that there is no cosmic scheme of things'; Kris Kristofferson's 'help me make it through the night' as popular Epicureanism; Carl Henry on God holding mankind accountable; the US Secretary for Education and the teaching of history; statistics - one in twenty-five NT verses on the return of Christ.
Thesis: 'You don't need an accurate chronology. You need a biblical theology. For a preoccupation with chronology, minus theology will give you nothing else than a mythology.'
Three points, announced up front: (1) the curiosity to be avoided, (2) the identity to be affirmed, (3) the strategy to be adopted.

1. Curiosity to be avoided (vv.1-3): Matthew 24:44 and Robert Murray McCheyne's Wednesday Bible study question 'do you think Jesus Christ will come today?'; Mark 13:32; Acts 1:6-8 'get off the hill, get into the streets'; three words - SECRET (the burglar who does not post you a card saying 'the Tuesday after next we will be burgling your house'; Begg's own house was burgled), SUDDEN (verse 3, and the Glasgow shoe-shop story of not knowing whether the Braxton Hicks were real), SEPARATION (Matthew 24:40-41).

Date-setters as cautionary tales: John Napier the inventor of logarithms projecting 1700 (23 editions between 1688 and 1700, 'since 1700 it has not been selling particularly well'); the Late Great Planet Earth; the 1784 prediction published in 1785.

2. Identity to be affirmed (vv.4-5): 'but you, brothers', generically used; Ephesians 5:8 and 1 Peter 2:9; the Shakespeare/Van Gogh illustration - 'if the genius of Van Gogh could come and live in me, I could paint that kind of picture'; a long attack on moralism and externalism, 'the identity is key to the activity'; 'if you shine, no need of sign'; the neon 'ADULT' sign on Interstate 71 at the base of which is total darkness.

3. Strategy to be adopted (v.6): 'so then'; gregoreo as the root of the name Gregory - 'let's all be Gregorys'; nepho, self-controlled; moral purity (1 John 3:3, 'you coming in my house... listening to my music, watching my videos') and zealous evangelism (John 9:4); 'Somebody gave me two books since last Sunday. I'm not reading them.'
VOLUME2/09 'The Coming of the Lord, Part Three' (1 Thess 5:6-11). Opens with the yellowed 1982 Times of London advertisement 'The Christ is now here' read out at length.

Since we belong to the day, three imperatives: STAY AWAKE (the ICU nurse; falling asleep at the wheel; the late flight to San Antonio because 'the pilot's asleep'; 1 Peter 5:8; Gethsemane), GUARD YOUR HEART (the breastplate of faith and love; the centurion who must not sleep when the city does; Ephesians 6 uses righteousness, here faith and love), KEEP YOUR HEAD (the helmet - 'Doesn't it scare you to see people screeching down the freeway on motorbikes without helmets?', extended and returned to at the close).

What God has done (vv.9-10): a full treatment of wrath as God's settled, non-capricious reaction to sin, grounded in Ephesians 2:3; 'it was the wrath of God that made Calvary necessary... it was the love of God that made Calvary a reality'; the fire brigade at the door in the middle of the night - 'we've come to rescue you' / 'but I don't need rescue'; imputation; 'My hope is built on nothing less'; Zinzendorf's 'Bold shall I stand in that great day'; Rock of Ages; the devil at 'the front door of your head' answered with 'while sin no longer reigns in my life, it remains'.

The implication (v.11): oikodomeo - building, mending nets, resetting fractured bones; 'Which of us emerges from the race of the Christian life without a few spikes in the shins?'; 'how are you fine, how are you fine, fine, fine'; 'commit yourself to being an encourager in Parkside Church'; encourage each other WITH THESE WORDS, i.e. with Scripture - Psalm 46 read down the phone to someone whose daughter has a tumour; the true pastor must be a good theologian.

Closing epigram: 'you'll never know who you are till you find out who he is. And some of you are spending all your time trying to find yourself and then you'll go look for him. I want to tell you, meet him. You'll find yourself.'
review.outline_comparison: Partly the same skeleton, for the obvious reason that both men are walking through 1 Thessalonians 5:1-11 in Paul's order: dates you cannot know, then 'but you, brothers, are sons of light', then the summons to alertness and the armour, then the wrath/salvation contrast, then 'encourage one another'. That sequence is Paul's, not Begg's. Below that shared verse order the two sermons share almost nothing. Begg announces a memorable three-point rhetorical scheme ('the curiosity to be avoided, the identity to be affirmed, the strategy to be adopted') and spends nearly a third of Part Two on a philosophy-of-history prologue with Lily Tomlin, Kris Kristofferson and Carl Henry; the FBC preacher has no prologue of that kind, uses a Haddon-Robinson-style single 'main idea' sentence which he states at [00:47:16] and repeats verbatim at [01:12:49], and organises the sermon around a modern 'how do you identify?' hook. Begg's three headings for verse 8 (stay awake, guard your heart, keep your head) have no counterpart at FBC, and Begg's two set-piece illustrations for that verse - the motorbike helmet and the centurion - are entirely absent from FBC, which instead uses a firefighter. Conversely FBC devotes six minutes to material Begg never touches: the chronos/kairos word study, the Galilean wedding, the three Greek senses of 'sleep', and an extended personal excursus on pre-trib/mid-trib/post-trib as a non-essential doctrine. They are even reading different translations - FBC works from the NASB ('as to the times and the epochs, brethren'), Begg from the NIV ('about times and dates... brothers') - which is why the only long shared word-strings in the whole comparison are Bible verses.

original_material.summary: Essentially the whole sermon is the preacher's own. A mechanical n-gram scan of the sermon window (4,421 words) against all twenty-two Begg transcripts returns not one shared seven-word string that is not Scripture: every hit is 1 Thess 4:16-17, 5:2, 5:5, 5:9 or 5:11, or 'died for us so that whether we', i.e. text both men are reading aloud. No Begg illustration, joke, commentator quote, epigram, transition or heading appears at FBC, and no FBC illustration appears in Begg. The preacher supplies his own hook (date-setting and Revelation), his own quoted authority (an unnamed researcher on ~300 failed predictions), his own humour (a self-consciously bad Armageddon pun), his own cultural framing (identity language borrowed from the contemporary gender debate and turned against it), his own liturgical habit (the congregational 2 Timothy 3:16 pledge, 'as is my normal practice'), two of his own family stories, a cross-reference back to his own earlier sermon series, his own word studies, a candid personal excursus in which he concedes he may be wrong about the timing of the rapture, and a local landing that ties the passage to the church's series title and to two named local outreaches.
examples: The rapture pun: 'I did think about beginning with a joke about the rapture, but I've decided I'm not going to do that... I'm not gonna do it because Armageddon's so tired of jokes like that' - followed by an audible flop and the preacher explaining it: 'Say it was Armageddon. I'm a you guys. I don't know. You didn't get it.' (0:44:59-0:45:18)

The identity hook reframed against contemporary gender discourse: 'The thrust of today's message and our time today is about identity. How do you identify? Now, before you do a knee-jerk reaction in our culture today, this is an overused question that speaks to gender. But not this message.' (0:45:21)

The congregational Bible pledge, a fixed personal ritual: 'as is my normal practice, I invite you to grab your Bible, your smartphone, your tablet... hold it up into the air and repeat after me this proclamation from 2 Timothy 3:16. The Bible is God's word...' with the congregation echoing each line (0:45:56-0:46:48)

Self-citation to his own earlier series: 'A couple of years ago, I taught a message about the significance in scripture of the Galilean wedding... you can find that series actually in your church center under the sermons... only the father of the groom knew when the wedding would take place' (0:53:24-0:54:11)

We knew the route to the hospital. We even had t-shirts made... and mine said coach on it' (0:56:50-0:57:12)

The firefighter illustration: 'how would you feel if you drove by a fire station with an open set of garage doors and you looked inside and you saw that the firefighters were sitting there in their pajamas on a lounge chair drinking a six-pack? ... Well, you're never going to see that. They are always ready' (1:00:45-1:01:35)

The three senses of 'sleep' in Greek and the hermeneutical moral: 'we kind of call it sleepwalking, don't we? ... But you know what else it can mean? Can mean no longer breathing, dead... So you see the context is what matters and defines what the interpretation is' (1:01:37-1:03:03)

Paul's method as a developing writer: 'in many cases, Paul would kind of float this new concept to the Thessalonica believers that he really doesn't give a whole lot of detail about. And then in other epistles written to other churches, he beefs it up' (1:04:37)

It's perfectly fine for you to believe something different than I believe on that... But here's the thing is I could be wrong. But the scripture remains.' (1:08:24-1:09:48)

review.rating_rationale: This sermon is genuinely independent of Begg and is the cleanest internal control in the corpus. The machine alignment is empty and my own seven-word n-gram scan of the sermon window against all twenty-two Begg transcripts produces only Scripture matches - 1 Thess 4:16-17, 5:2, 5:5, 5:9-11 - which is exactly what two preachers reading the same passage should produce and is not evidence of anything. The two men are not even using the same translation: FBC reads the NASB ('as to the times and the epochs, brethren'), Begg the NIV ('about times and dates... brothers'), so a preacher working from Begg's manuscript would have had to re-key every quotation. Every load-bearing illustration is different and, more tellingly, Begg's most memorable ones are missing precisely where a dependent sermon would have used them: at verse 8 Begg spends four minutes on the motorbike helmet and returns to it as his closing image, while FBC disposes of the helmet in a single clause and reaches for a firefighter instead; at verse 3 both preachers tell a first-child labour story, but FBC's is a go bag and a T-shirt reading 'coach' in an American hospital and Begg's is Braxton Hicks in a Glasgow shoe shop. The FBC preacher also does several things Begg never does anywhere in the series - a chronos/kairos word study, the Galilean wedding, a congregational 2 Timothy 3:16 pledge, and a candid admission that he may be wrong about the timing of the rapture - and the one quotation he does borrow, the unnamed researcher's tally of roughly 300 failed date predictions, has no counterpart in Begg, whose date-setting examples are Napier, Hal Lindsey and a 1784 prediction published in 1785. The only convergences are the ones the text itself forces: both make identity the theme of verses 4-5, both note that 'sons' is generic and includes daughters, and both cross-reference the armour to Ephesians 6 - observations available in any commentary and reached here in different words, different order and different company.

caveats: The alignment file for this sermon is empty (0.0% coverage) and the best machine scores were 1.65% and below, i.e. noise; 'region_classification' is therefore {} by design, not by omission.

All shared word-strings I could find between this sermon and any Begg transcript are Bible text that both preachers read aloud (1 Thess 4:16-17, 5:2, 5:5, 5:9-11). Under the brief's rule, Scripture read aloud by both is not evidence of borrowing, and here it is literally the only overlap.

The captions are YouTube auto-generated and mangle proper nouns and Greek: 'Kronos'/'chyros' for chronos/kairos, 'Thessalon Thessalonica', 'Kellon'/'Kelland' for the same elementary school, 'grieavves' for 'grieves', 'Ephesians 6:es 10-18', 'livinging hope' in the song lyrics. Quoted excerpts preserve the caption text verbatim; occasional capitalised runs (e.g. 'FOR YOU YOURSELVES KNOW FULL well') are a caption artefact, not emphasis.

There are no [music] tags in this file. I identified the songs by their lyric content and repeated refrains ('I'm no longer a slave to fear', 'Living Hope', 'Great Are You Lord', 'Hallelujah', 'Choose Joy'); every one of them falls outside the 0:42:55-1:14:01 sermon window.

Some overlap of ideas is unavoidable and generic: 'the day of the Lord comes like a thief', 'sons of light', 'not appointed to wrath', armour language, and the pairing of 1 Thess 5 with Matthew 24 and Ephesians 6 are standard evangelical stock and appear in every commentary on the passage. I have treated none of these as evidence.

Two speakers must be kept apart in any report drawn from this file: the sermon (0:42:55-1:14:01) is preached by the rotating teacher whose wife is Sheila, while the invitation at 1:18:52-1:26:04 - including the Kurt and Ace story and the sinner's prayer - is Pastor Pat, the lead pastor, whose wife is Cindy. That closing segment was not assessed as part of this sermon.

Because this file is being used as the study's internal control, the relevant claim is narrow: this preacher, on this passage, on this date, is not using Begg. It says nothing about the other FBC sermons in the playlist, several of which are preached by different men.

outline_fbc: Framing: our culture's twisted view of 'influence' -- the social-media influencer dream; influence as self-benefit vs. biblical influence for others; Simon Sinek's 'influence is not about elevating yourself but about lifting others' (0:44:50)

Main idea stated: 'God's will is for his people, not only for personal spiritual devotion, but for having a spirit-shaped community that is marked by respect, by care, by goodness and joy, by prayer, gratitude and discernment, and holiness' (0:46:24)
Reading of 1 Thessalonians 5:12-22 straight through (0:46:55)

1. Honor those who serve the Lord (vv.12-13): recognize their labor / respect their spiritual responsibility / esteem them very highly -- Greek 'perissos' cross-referenced to the crucify-him crowd and to Ephesians 3:20; payoff = 'you will be at peace among yourselves'; application question 'do I make ministry easier or harder for those who serve?' (0:49:03)

2. Minister to people according to their need (v.14): Jesus ministered differently every time -- soft, firm, nurturing, exhortation, rebuke; warn the idle/disruptive, encourage the fainthearted ('needing courage placed back into their heart'), help the weak, be patient with everyone because 1 Corinthians 13 makes 'love is patient' the first word of the definition (0:54:02)

3. Choose good over getting even (v.15): refuse retaliation; 'the next time you're wrong, instead of saying how can I get back at them, ask what would good look like in this situation?' -- and it is there that 'we become influential' (0:59:04)

4. Practice the will of God daily (vv.16-18): rejoice always (not denying the pain); pray without ceasing -- three concepts drawn from the Lord's Prayer: worship of God, daily needs, intercession for others (1:03:35); give thanks in all circumstances, supported by James 1:2-4 and Romans 5:3-5 'hope does not disappoint' (1:05:45)

5. What is God's will for me? -- the question is usually asked about job/marriage/big purchase while ignoring what God has already clearly revealed; God's will is in daily habits, not only big decisions (1:07:12)

6. Discern what is from God and hold fast to good (vv.19-22): don't quench the Spirit (camping fire-pit image); an audit -- 'Let's test it' -- showing every earlier command, if disobeyed, could quench the Spirit (1:10:27); don't despise prophecies (Strong's definition of 'propheta'; the Bible itself meets the definition, so preaching can be prophetic utterance); test everything like the Bereans of Acts 17; hold fast to good; abstain from evil (1:08:39)
Song break: 'I ask for you to just contemplate these thoughts, these concepts as we sing this next song' (1:15:18); 'Goodness of God' 1:15:49-1:19:24

Recap of the main idea and five application questions -- honor those who serve? encourage someone weak or weary? let go of revenge? return to joy, prayer, thanksgiving? test what you're hearing and hold fast? (1:19:33)
Closing prayer, including 'this place of darkness where even the word influence has become self-corrupted' (1:21:23)
outline_begg: Begg does NOT preach 1 Thess 5:12-22 as one message. In source_transcripts/volume3 he takes the same ten verses across NINE consecutive sermons, each with its own text, structure and cross-references:

01 'Learning to Respect Our Leadership' (5:12-13): two heads -- (a) the activity of the leaders (they work hard among you / they are over you in the Lord / they admonish you) and (b) the attitude of the members (respect them; hold them in the highest regard in love). Extended digressions on elder plurality, congregational vs. elder government, women not serving as elders, 1 Timothy 3 household management, the flattery-is-like-perfume line, the 'don't call the pastor a star' rant, and the moved-chair/biblical-mandate-vs-personal-preference peroration.

02 'Learning to Live in Peace' (5:13b): 'live in peace with each other' via the Living Bible's 'remember no quarreling among yourselves'; the family-car-trip illustration; discord in a family is not impossible, just incongruous; a catalogue of the individuals involved (the idle, the timid, the weak).

03 'Practicing Patience' (5:14-15a): read against Matthew 18's unforgiving servant; patience as (a) a divine attribute and (b) a Christian virtue; the DMV, fast-food lines and green traffic lights; the 'Herbert the snail / have patience' children's tape; then 'renounce retaliation' with the soccer-tackle image, Romans 12:19, 1 Cor 4:12, the USA Today 'justifiable homicide' abortion-clinic quote, the prodigal son, and the John Harper/Titanic poem 'If we but knew'.
04 'Cultivating Kindness' (5:15b): read against the Good Samaritan; the Philip Seldon 'revenge classes' newspaper article; kindness as steady commitment, not intermittent bursts.

05 'Learning How to Worship: An Introduction' (5:16-17): argues at length that vv.16-22 concern PUBLIC worship (the verbs are plural); three things about which God is never indifferent, beginning with whether we worship at all; every culture is a worshiping culture; Romans 1:25.

06 'Give Thanks' (5:18): 'the directive' and 'the doctrine which underpins the directive'; thankfulness is unnatural; the Anglican prayer book's general thanksgiving; the Coke/7-Up 'what spills out when you bump into someone' image; the qualifier 'in all circumstances'; the doctrine of PROVIDENCE (Westminster Shorter Catechism Q11), Cowper's 'behind a frowning providence he hides a smiling face', 'flying the instruments', Genesis 22 Jehovah-Jireh.

07 'Do Not Grieve the Holy Spirit' (5:19): a full doctrinal excursus -- no one is a Christian unless the Spirit indwells them; the Spirit is a person, not an it; therefore he can be grieved; the impassibility of God; offending against God's LOVE rather than God's law; the silent-car-ride marriage illustration; then three ways we quench the fire -- starve it of fuel, douse it with water, cover it with dirt.

08 'Listening to the Word of God' (5:20-21): 'never despise what is spoken in the name of the Lord' (J.B. Phillips); John Stott quoted; no living apostles/foundational prophets; 'test everything' = dokimazo, the BSA windscreen-approval sticker; three tests -- the test of Scripture itself, the test of the person of Jesus, the test of the gospel of free grace; Deuteronomy 13; Jude; Walter Martin and 'the kingdom of the cults'.
09 'Sanctification' and 10 'The Faithfulness of God' (5:22-24) close the series.
review.outline_comparison: Different -- structurally, exegetically and rhetorically. FBC compresses all ten verses into one 35-minute message hung on a single unifying theme announced at the top ('a life of influence' / 'a spirit-shaped community'), with six numbered movements and an application question after each; Begg spends nine sermons on the same ten verses and never uses 'influence' as an organizing idea at all. Where FBC and Begg touch the same verse they take different routes: on vv.12-13 FBC's three-part 'recognize their labor / respect their spiritual responsibility / esteem them very highly' with a Greek word study of 'perissos' tied to Ephesians 3:20 has nothing in common with Begg's 'activity of the leaders / attitude of the members' and his long polemic on church government; on v.18 FBC reaches for James 1 and Romans 5 while Begg reaches for the doctrine of providence and Cowper; on v.19 FBC gives one campfire image and then an audit of the preceding verses, while Begg gives a doctrine-of-the-Spirit lecture including divine impassibility. The only genuinely shared skeleton is the order of Paul's own imperatives, which is fixed by the text itself.

original_material.summary: Effectively the whole sermon is the FBC preacher's own. Nothing outside the quoted biblical text can be traced to Begg's 1 Thessalonians series or to any other file in source_transcripts/. His frame (the 'influencer' culture critique), his supporting texts (Matthew 5, Acts 2, 2 Timothy 3:16, Ephesians 3:20, Ephesians 4:3, 1 Corinthians 13, James 1:2-4, Romans 5:3-5, the Lord's Prayer, Acts 17), his word studies (perissos, propheta via Strong's), his one named non-biblical source (Simon Sinek), his humour, his congregational call-and-response, his self-deprecation about preaching vv.12-13, his personal testimony about temptation, and his local-church application are all absent from Begg. Structurally he does something Begg never does: after teaching vv.19-22 he loops back and audits every preceding command against 'could this quench the Holy Spirit?' -- a genuinely original organising move that welds the whole passage into one argument.

review.rating_rationale: This sermon is independent of Alistair Begg. The machine alignment found no paired source above threshold, and a direct 5-gram comparison of the sermon window (5,269 tokens) against all thirty Begg files returns only Scripture and dead-generic filler: the longest shared strings anywhere in the corpus are 'give thanks in all circumstances', 'this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus', 'live in peace with one another' and 'in love because of their work' -- i.e. 1 Thessalonians 5:13-18 itself, which both men read aloud, plus phrases like 'read the word of God' and 'I want to do it'. Targeted greps for the sermon's distinctive load-bearing material (Simon Sinek / 'start with the why' / 'elevating yourself'; perissos; Ephesians 3:20 'far more abundantly'; Strong's / propheta; 'prophetic utterance'; the Bereans of Acts 17 used as a testing model; James 1 'consider it all joy'; Romans 5 'hope does not disappoint'; the fire-pit; 'free time career' / 'rounds of golf'; 'look to your neighbor') return ZERO hits across source_transcripts/volume1, volume2 and volume3. Not one Begg signature -- 'loved ones', J.B. Phillips, John Stott, Parkside, the flattery-is-like-perfume line, the Herbert-the-snail tape, providence and Cowper, the impassibility of God -- appears. The two superficial contacts are both dictated by the text rather than by a source: both preachers picture fire and water because Paul wrote 'quench', and both restate Paul's imperatives in Paul's order. As an internal control this sermon is valuable precisely because it shows what an independent FBC treatment of 1 Thessalonians looks like: same book, same verses, same week-by-week series, and essentially zero lexical contact with Begg.
report_quotes: CONTRAST, same verse (5:13, 'esteem them very highly') -- FBC (0:51:48): 'And the phrase very highly, it means so much more than just very highly. In the Greek, this word is peros ... It means exceedingly abundantly over overthe-top, passionately, without wavering.' | BEGG (01-learningtorespectourleadership): 'to respect does not mean to flatter or to fawn over them, nobody wants that ... told you before flattery is like perfume you can sniff it but don't ever swallow it.'

CONTRAST, same verse (5:19, 'do not quench the Spirit') -- FBC (1:09:09): 'quench is a term that is often used as it pertains to fire. So if you were out camping and you were using a fire pit well before you went to your tent at night ... You would douse it with water. And in this way, Paul is saying, don't throw water on the Holy Spirit.' | BEGG (07-donotgrievetheholyspirit): 'This is how we'll quench the fire of the spirit in our lives. Three ways, essentially. Number one, starve the fire of fuel ... Secondly, if I douse it with water ... And thirdly, if I cover the fire up with dirt.' -- the shared word is 'douse'; the shared idea is Paul's own metaphor; the structures and applications are unrelated.

ORIGINAL FRAME with no Begg counterpart -- FBC (0:45:43): 'Even a guy named Simon Synynic, yes, that's really his name ... He said this influence is not about elevating yourself but about lifting others. He knew that. He probably got it from Paul.' | BEGG: no equivalent anywhere -- 'influence', 'influencer' and 'Sinek' return no hits in any of the thirty source transcripts.
caveats: Both preachers read 1 Thessalonians 5:12-22 aloud, so every long shared string in the comparison is Scripture and is not evidence of borrowing. They also read different translations -- FBC uses a NASB-family text ('we request of you, brethren ... esteem them very highly in love because of their work'), Begg uses the NIV ('we ask you brothers ... hold them in the highest regard in love because of their work') -- which further reduces even accidental overlap.

Restating Paul's imperatives in Paul's order (honour leaders -> warn/encourage/help/be patient -> no revenge -> rejoice/pray/give thanks -> don't quench/don't despise/test/hold fast/abstain) is dictated by the text and is not shared structure in any meaningful sense.
The fire-and-water imagery at v.19 is generated by the verb 'quench' itself and is used by almost every expositor of this verse; the coincidence of the word 'douse' in both is weak-to-nil evidence.

FBC's 'not a full-time career but more a free time career ... daily rounds of golf' and Begg's 'lazy rascals who seem to spend most of their days wearing slippers ... rarely get out of their pajamas' are both instances of the stock pastoral joke about how easy congregations imagine ministry to be. No wording is shared and the two do different work in their respective sermons (FBC sets up 'spiritual leadership is real work'; Begg is warning the elders themselves).

The FBC transcript is YouTube auto-captions and contains obvious ASR errors that must be quoted with care: 'Simon Synynic' (Simon Sinek), 'peros' / 'Perisos' / 'parasos' (perissos), 'propheta' (propheteia), 'the Thessalon people', 'disciplehip', 'helping of the week' (weak), 'pray without pe uh ceasing', 'James, the halfb brotherther of Jesus', 'the gig stats'. The Begg transcripts are Whisper ASR and contain their own errors ('weirdism toil' for wearisome toil, 'Kaupur' for Cowper, 'Samist' for Psalmist, 'Dokey must' for dokimazo), so exact-string matching in either direction understates true overlap slightly -- but the gap here is far too large for ASR noise to explain.

The alignment file analysis/out/alignments/The_Walk_of_Influence_-_071926_EuKaZ_afxRo.txt contains no regions (0.0% fuzzy coverage, paired sources: []), so region_classification is intentionally empty.
Common evangelical stock phrases present in both corpora ('the word of God', 'the power of the Holy Spirit', 'a body of believers', 'God's will for you') carry no evidential weight.

review.speaker_notes: Two voices. The service host/announcer identifies himself at 0:14:35: "If I haven't met you yet, I'm Pastor Kevin" — he does the announcements, the closing remarks (1:24:56) and the benediction, but he does NOT preach. The preacher is a different man who takes the platform at 0:43:23 ("man getting Pentecostal already, okay, that's great"). He refers to Pastor Kevin in the third person as the previous week's preacher (0:45:02 "Last message in 1 Thessalonians chapter 5 verses 16-22, Pastor Kevin left us with some bite-sized chunks"), names his wife twice ("Cindy's car" 0:46:03; "Cindy's out of town" 0:59:48), speaks of "the life of a pastor, against the life of me" (0:59:27), and in his closing prayer quotes God addressing him by name: "I know you said to me even about this, 'Watch me work, Pat. Watch me work'" (1:15:13) — so the preacher is Pastor Pat. Audience cues are strongly local and interactive: call-and-response ("Say that with me" 0:44:15; "Now, let's say it out loud. God is for me" 1:05:20), a show-of-hands moment, Tucson references (a photo taken driving "from Phoenix through Eloy" in monsoon rain, 0:46:41), the church's "big mess" back-to-school event, and "God is for our church" (1:06:31).
review.boundary_note: The worship set and the worship leader's prayer end at 0:43:16 with the congregational "amen" at 0:43:20. The preacher's first words are at 0:43:23 ("man getting Pentecostal already okay that's great, I'm a little bit loud on the mic"), immediately followed by "open your Bibles to 1 Thessalonians 5" (0:43:33) and his reading of 5:23-24, so the opening banter plus the scripture reading are counted as the start of the sermon proper. He says "Let's pray" at 1:14:22; the closing pastoral prayer runs to its last words "So I'm watching, Lord" at 1:15:20, after which the band re-enters at 1:15:54 with "Worthy is the Lamb." Everything before 0:43:23 (four worship songs, announcements about the "big mess" event, offering prayer) and everything after 1:15:20 (three songs, Pastor Kevin's closing remarks and benediction, exit music) is service, not sermon.
review.passage: 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24, expounded almost entirely through Romans 8:1, 31-35 (with Romans 4:23-25, 5:1, 7:24, Philippians 1:6 and 1 John 3:2 brought in)

attribution.notes: The preacher never names Alistair Begg, Truth For Life, or any sermon he consulted. Not once does he use a borrowing signal such as "I read," "one preacher said," "as someone has put it," or "I'm indebted to." Everything is delivered in his own first person, including material that is Begg's own first-person testimony: at 0:56:23 he says "And that's been true this week. At least for me, it's been very true this week that I haven't done all the good that I long to do" — Begg's line is "And that's been true this week. It has for me. I have not lived and done all the good for which I longed." The only citations he does give (Westminster Confession, Zinzendorf, Phillips, "Jer"/Packer) are precisely the four secondary sources Begg cites, cited at the same points in the same argument, which suggests the citations themselves came from Begg rather than from independent reading. Note also that at 0:52:45 he attributes to "1 Thessalonians 5:4" a sentence that is actually Begg's own summary ("the experience of all real Christians, everyone and at all times"), i.e. Begg's commentary has been mistaken for the text.

outline_fbc: Text read: 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24 (0:43:33)

Announced four points, "four nutrients": 1) consider God's faithfulness expressed in the love of God; 2) reckon God's faithfulness in the face of accusation; 3) reflect on God's faithfulness in light of the provision of his son; 4) behold God's faithfulness as it's expressed in the love of Christ (0:44:02-0:44:39)
Opening images of the daily grind — chewed homework, a broken transmission, an anchor, rain crowned by a rainbow (photo taken driving through Eloy) (0:45:53-0:47:01)

Point 1: 'blameless at his coming' — the word Paul uses only here; Thessalonian tombstones; the day of completion; 1 John 3:2; Philippians 1:6; Zinzendorf's hymn; the 'what/how question'; verse 24 as the answer; Phillips' rendering; God is not the author of unfinished business (0:47:01-0:53:28)
Turn to Romans 8: no condemnation (v1) to no separation (v39); the progression of Romans 1-5 (0:53:28-0:55:24)

Point 2: reckon God's faithfulness in the face of accusation — Westminster Confession's 'continual irreconcilable war'; 'that's been true this week'; Romans 7:24; Pogo, 'we have met the enemy and he is us'; Romans 8:1; the onslaught of hell; the flat-tire story; Packer's list of troubled Christians; where do I ground my assurance; feelings vs theology; Johnny Cochran / Robert Shapiro; 'If God is for us'; 'God is for me'; God's decision to justify cannot be altered; sleeping like a baby; McCain joke; 'you don't understand me the way God understands me'; don't let the enemy drag you back into the garbage can (0:55:24-1:10:39)
Point 3: reflect on God's faithfulness in the light of the provision of his son — Romans 8:32; the bicycle with no pedals (1:10:22-1:11:48)
Point 4: behold God's faithfulness expressed in the love of Christ — Romans 8:35, 38; why do we still believe? God's faithfulness (1:11:48-1:12:50)

Re-reading of 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24 and the application: 'If God is for me, carve that into your mind today'; the car mechanic exchange; 'One thing I know for sure, God is for you and he's for me' (1:12:50-1:14:22)
Closing prayer (1:14:22-1:15:20)
outline_begg: Continuing from the morning message; the last two of four points on 1 Thess 5:23-24: the product that emerges from the process, and the promise by which he assures them

The product: 'kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ' — the only occasion Paul employs this word; Thessalonican tombstones bearing 'holoclerus'; cross-reference to 3:13; a day of entirety and completeness; 1 John 3:2; 'in the present we are under construction'; Philippians 1:6; Zinzendorf's hymn ('bold shall I stand'; 'this spotless robe'); the 'what question, the how question, the can it possibly be question'
The promise (v24): 'the one who calls you is faithful and he will do it' — or in Phillips, 'utterly faithful ... will finish what he has set out to do'; God is not the author of unfinished business

Turn to Romans 8 to expound it: no condemnation (v1) to no separation (v39); the progression of Romans 1-5; the Westminster Confession's 'continual and irreconcilable war'; 'that's been true this week ... it has for me'; Romans 7:24; Romans 8:1

All-round righteousness meets all-round pressure; the total onslaught of hell; Packer's list of troubled Christians; 'how then am I to cope? Where may I turn? ... the answer is in the faithfulness of God'; evangelical thinking correcting emotional thinking
Four sub-points from Romans 8: (a) v31 God is for us — 'one of the great four words statements'; personalise it: 'God is for me'
(b) v32 God's faithfulness in the giving of his Son; Psalm 84:11

(c) v33 God's faithfulness in the face of accusation — God decided to justify you and knew everything; nobody can produce new evidence of your depravity; 'this is the way to sleep like a baby at night'; 'you don't understand me the way God understands me'; don't let the devil drag you back to the garbage cans; Augustus Toplady's hymn

(d) v35 God's faithfulness expressed in the love of Christ; the dandelion 'he loves me, he loves me not'; 1 Peter 1:5; 'you are not strong enough to fall away while God is resolved to hold you'; Romans 8:38-39
Close: 'carve it into your recollection as you begin tomorrow morning ... God is for me'; Toplady, 'the work which his goodness began'; 'Take my life and let it be'
review.outline_comparison: Same skeleton, lightly reordered and re-verbed. Both men take 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24, work the identical sequence inside it (the rare word 'blameless at his coming' and the Thessalonian tombstones, 1 John 3:2, Philippians 1:6, Zinzendorf's two hymn stanzas, the 'what/how question', verse 24 answered in the Phillips translation, 'God is not the author of unfinished business'), then make the same pivot — 'how can we be sure of this? Turn to this great chapter,' Romans 8 — and run the same 'no condemnation to no separation' frame, the same Romans 1-5 recap, the same Westminster Confession line, the same Packer list, and the same four sub-points drawn from Romans 8:31, 32, 33, 35. The only structural change is that FBC promotes Begg's four Romans 8 sub-points into the sermon's headline outline announced at 0:44:02, swaps the order of provision (v32) and accusation (v33), and replaces Begg's fourfold repeated verb 'consider' with an alliterative-ish consider / reckon / reflect / behold. Begg's Toplady material, his Psalm 84:11, his dandelion illustration and his 1 Peter section are dropped; FBC substitutes his own illustrations in those slots.

And fourth, the best, behold God's faithfulness as it's expressed in the love of Christ.

The wording of headings 1, 3 and 4 tracks Begg almost word for word; only the verbs vary.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher supplies his own opening (a run of 'daily grind' images and a personal photograph), his own illustrations in most of the slots where Begg had illustrations, congregational interaction, and his own closing prayer. Crucially, ALL of his substitutions sit inside Begg's frame: they decorate Begg's points, they never generate a point. Where Begg has Augustus Toplady's hymn twice, the dandelion 'he loves me, he loves me not', Psalm 84:11, 1 Peter 1:5 and the Packer aphorism 'you are not strong enough to fall away while God is resolved to hold you', FBC substitutes Pogo, a flat bicycle tyre, O.J. Simpson's defence team, John McCain on the Tonight Show, a bicycle without pedals, and 'Let's get ready to rumble'. He also adds a few genuinely his own theological touches — 'There's a difference between being innocent and blameless', the 'just as if I'd never sinned' wordplay on justification, the extra step of contrasting feelings AND logic with theology (Begg contrasts only emotional with evangelical thinking), and an actual quotation of 1 John 3:2 where Begg only paraphrases it. The exegesis, the argument, the sequence, the secondary citations and the conclusion are Begg's.
examples: The 'daily grind' image set — chewed homework, 'a battlefield', 'I just survived taking Cindy's car in to find out the transmission is broke', shadows scattering light, an anchor tethering one firm in a storm (0:45:53-0:46:35)

A personal photograph: 'Rain crowned by a rainbow. A couple weeks ago, I took this picture. I was driving from Phoenix through Eloy during one of these monsoons that we've been having' (0:46:35-0:47:01) — local Tucson colour, entirely his own

Walt Kelly's Pogo: 'On April 22nd, 1971, a cartoonist by the name of Walt Kelly had a character named Pogo ... We have met the enemy and he is us' (0:56:57-0:57:34), with his own turn 'the first enemy that you have to deal with is neither someone else or even the devil itself ... It's you'
The flat-tyre-and-lost-phone story: 'I got on a bicycle Saturday to ride and within five minutes I had a flat tire ... it isn't about falling. It's about getting up' (0:59:46-1:00:32)

The O.J. Simpson defence-team riff: 'God is our Johnny Cochran. God is our Robert Shapiro ... Do you need Johnny Cochran to say if it don't fit it must have quit?' (1:03:54-1:04:26) — congregational Q&A, distinctively American, no counterpart in Begg
The John McCain / Jay Leno 'I slept like a baby' joke (1:08:36-1:08:53), grafted onto Begg's borrowed 'sleep like a baby' line

The bicycle-with-no-pedals illustration for Romans 8:32: 'It's a great bike, but there's no pedals. Well, Dad, where's the pedals? ... He's going to give you the pedals' (1:10:42-1:11:41) — replaces Begg's Psalm 84:11

Wordplay: 'like that announcer before the big wrestling matches. Let's get ready to rumble. Well, let's get ready to reckon' (1:10:07-1:10:22); and 'We're justified in Christ. It's just as if I'd never sinned' (1:02:46)
'There's a difference between being innocent and blameless' (1:05:43) — his own distinction, not in Begg

Local/congregational application: 'God is for our church' (1:06:31), the mechanic exchange 'if a broken transmission is the worst thing that happens to me, man, I'm a blessed person' (1:13:55), and the closing prayer naming his own besetting sin of judging others and 'Watch me work, Pat' (1:14:22-1:15:20)

personalisation_patterns: Begg's evening service becomes a Sunday morning: 'it is true tonight concerning you' becomes 'It's true for you this morning' (1:04:58); 'Tonight we face animosity' becomes 'So what's going on today? Today we might face animosity' (1:05:55).

Begg's British idiom is Americanised: 'garbage cans of sins' stays but 'the devil' becomes 'the enemy' (1:09:49); 'brighten up ... shape up ... shut up' becomes 'time to brighten it up. Time to shape up ... time to shut up' (1:07:34).

Begg's single repeated verb 'consider' across four Romans 8 sub-points is varied into a preachable quartet — consider / reckon / reflect / behold — and promoted to the sermon's announced outline (0:44:02).

Begg's first-person testimony is re-owned rather than attributed: 'It has for me. I have not lived and done all the good for which I longed' becomes 'At least for me, it's been very true this week that I haven't done all the good that I long to do' (0:56:23).

Statements are converted into congregational participation: Begg's 'take this and take it to yourself. God is for us' becomes 'Take this and take it for yourself and say this to yourself first. God is for me. Now, let's say it out loud. God is for me' (1:05:13); and the outline itself is turned into a call-and-response, 'Say that with me' (0:44:15).

Begg's illustrations are swapped for American pop-culture equivalents in the same rhetorical slots: Toplady's hymns become Pogo and Johnny Cochran; the dandelion becomes the bicycle pedals; the plain 'sleep like a baby' becomes a John McCain talk-show joke.
Begg's declarative assertions become rhetorical questions to the room: 'Who can bring a charge against you?' becomes 'Guess who it is? It's you' (0:57:44) and 'Are you guilty before God?' (1:04:13).

Precision is loosened, sometimes into error: Begg's careful 'the experience of all real Christians everywhere and at all times' is reassigned by FBC to a verse — 'Paul is affirming this in 1 Thessalonians 5:4' (0:52:45) — a citation that does not say that.
review.rating_rationale: This is not influence; it is a re-preached manuscript. The FBC sermon follows Begg's 'The Faithfulness of God' from its opening exegetical claim (the hapax 'blameless at his coming' and the Thessalonican tombstones) through its pivot to Romans 8 ('how can we be sure of this? Turn to this great chapter'), its Romans 1-5 recap, its Westminster Confession citation, its Packer list, its four Romans 8 sub-points, and out through its final take-home line ('carve that into your mind ... one thing I know for sure, God is for me') — the same ideas, in the same order, in very largely the same words. The machine found 31% of the sermon window in near-verbatim alignment, and that undercounts, because the un-aligned stretches are mostly FBC illustrations inserted into slots that Begg's outline created. Every secondary source the preacher cites (Zinzendorf, Phillips, the Westminster Confession, 'Jer'/Packer) is a source Begg cites at the same moment, and several borrowings carry transmission damage — a dropped negation, a dangling 'which he then abandons', a stumble over 'the great four-word statements' — which shows recitation rather than composition. Begg and Truth For Life are never named, and no borrowing signal of any kind is given; Begg's own 'that's been true this week ... for me' confession is delivered as the preacher's own. I withhold a 10 only because the delivery is genuinely re-voiced, roughly a third of the airtime is his own illustration and local application, and a handful of small theological touches ('there's a difference between being innocent and blameless') are his.
report_quotes: FBC (0:56:23): "And that's been true this week. At least for me, it's been very true this week that I haven't done all the good that I long to do." | BEGG: "And that's been true this week. It has for me. I have not lived and done all the good for which I longed."

FBC (1:09:24): "The only thing is you don't understand me the way God understands me. And frankly, it's just as well because if you understood me to the depth that God does, you'd never talk to me again. ... Don't let the enemy drag you back into the garbage can of your sins. They've been settled at Calvary long ago. ... Hide in the faithfulness of God." | BEGG: "But the only thing is you don't understand me the way God understands me. And frankly, it's just as well ... Because if you understood me to the depth that He does, you'd never talk to me again. ... Don't allow the devil to drag you back to the garbage cans of sins that have been settled at Calvary long ago. ... Hide in the faithfulness of God."

FBC (1:13:33): "If God is for me, carve that into your mind today. ... One thing I know for sure, God is for you and he's for me." | BEGG: "carve it into your recollection as you begin tomorrow morning ... say this to yourself, well I know one thing for sure, God is for me."
caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captioning of a live room with a hot mic, and the Begg text is Whisper ASR of an audio archive; both mangle proper nouns. 'Count Ludri von Zeninsorf' is Zinzendorf, 'holocaros'/'holoclerus' is holokleros, 'Jer put it so eloquently' is almost certainly 'J.I. Packer put it so eloquently' (Begg's transcript renders the same name 'Packard'), and 'Jay Lyn' is Jay Leno. Word-level identity scores should therefore be read as floors, not ceilings.

1 Thessalonians 5:23-24 is the preaching text for both men, so every occurrence of 'the one who calls you is faithful and he will do it' (alignment regions 1-3, 9-11) is Scripture read aloud and is NOT evidence of borrowing. The same applies to the shared quotations of Philippians 1:6, 1 John 3:2, Romans 4:23-25, 7:24, 8:1, 8:31-35. The machine's small overlap with volume2/02-sexualpuritypartone.txt is entirely of this kind: that sermon quotes 1 Thess 5:23-24 in full while looking ahead to chapter 5, and nothing in the FBC sermon matches its surrounding commentary. It should be disregarded.

The machine's Scripture labels on several regions are wrong and were re-judged by hand: region 24 ('what are we going to say to it, what are we going to do') is tagged 'Exodus 16' but is Begg's rhetoric, and regions 1-3/9-11 are tagged 'Daniel 11' but are 1 Thessalonians 5:24.

Some overlapping language is genuine evangelical stock and carries little weight on its own: 'filthy rags', 'fiery darts of the evil one', 'we are under construction', 'no condemnation ... no separation' as a summary of Romans 8. These were not counted as findings; the case rests on the exegetical claims, the secondary citations, the first-person confession, the Packer list, the four-point structure and the peroration.

The two men have different sermon economies: Begg's is an evening exposition ending in Toplady and 'Take my life and let it be'; FBC's is a Sunday-morning message with congregational response, a local-event tie-in and a pastoral prayer. The re-voicing is real. The judgement here is about the substance and its order, not about delivery.

I checked the other eighteen Begg transcripts in source_transcripts/ for the FBC sermon's non-aligned material. Nothing else matched: 'garbage cans of sin' also appears in volume3/09-sanctification.txt, but that is Begg reusing his own phrase, and the FBC context (Romans 8:33, accusation) matches volume3/10 rather than 09. Pogo, Walt Kelly, Johnny Cochran, Robert Shapiro, John McCain, the bicycle pedals, the rainbow photograph and 'let's get ready to rumble' appear nowhere in the Begg corpus and should be treated as the FBC preacher's own.

[00:30:26.080] with the kids' 'Amen' at [00:30:29.080]. After that it is purely dismissal by colour group to the messy games. Talk length is roughly 8 minutes; the video's remaining audio is ambient.

review.outline_comparison: Not comparable. No Begg source was paired with this item by the machine (the alignment file records 'paired sources: []' and 0.0% coverage), and there is no Begg 1 Thessalonians sermon that this children's talk parallels. The FBC content is a stock kids' gospel presentation built around a water-and-colour object lesson; Begg's 1 Thessalonians series is expository verse-by-verse preaching to adults. The skeletons share nothing beyond the universal evangelical sin/cross/forgiveness sequence.

original_material.summary: The entire item is independent of Begg. It is a Saturday children's event talk: an interactive 'grossest thing' opener tied to the day's toilet-paper and messy-games theme, a map/path definition of sin, and a live water-discolouration-and-clearing object lesson, all pitched at kindergarten through fifth grade. The only material that is not the speaker's own is generic evangelical gospel content and loose Scripture allusion, which is not evidence of borrowing from anyone.
examples: Interactive kid Q&A with real-time answers from the room ('Yeah, broccoli. Broccoli?' / 'He hates tomatoes. My son.') (0:22:43)
'And it's just like tracking sticky mud all over a clean floor' - an image tied to the day's messy-games theme (0:24:05)
'Think of God's plan like a map showing us the safest, happiest, or the most blessed road to take. Sin is simply whenever you decide to step off that path' (0:24:42)

Live object lesson with water: 'Does the water look clear and pure?' ... 'Looks reddish, it looks kind of yucky. You wouldn't want to drink that, would you?' ... 'How does the water look now?' (0:25:47 - 0:28:31)
Extemporaneous closing prayer: 'Lord, so forgive us. And in the same breath I say thank you for forgiving us.' (0:30:07)

review.rating_rationale: There is no Begg material here at all, so the rating is 0. The machine alignment file confirms it: no Begg source was even paired with this video and fuzzy coverage is 0.0%. Reading the whole transcript shows why - this is not a Sunday sermon but a Saturday children's ministry event led by Brian, the family ministry director, with an unnamed female co-host, for kids in kindergarten through fifth grade divided into colour teams for 'messy games'. The talk is roughly eight minutes long, expounds no passage (certainly not 1 Thessalonians), and consists of a warm-up question, a water-and-colour object lesson, and a gospel invitation. I also grepped distinctive phrases ('sticky mud', 'toilet paper', 'messy') across all twenty-two Begg source transcripts and found only one irrelevant coincidence ('no messy muck on their bottles of oil' in volume3/04-cultivatingkindness.txt). This item should be excluded from the comparison set: it is a different speaker, a different day, a different audience, and a different genre.
caveats: Auto-generated YouTube captions; speaker turns ('>>') are unreliable and the two hosts' lines are frequently interleaved, so attribution of individual sentences between Brian and his co-host is approximate. The gospel talk from 0:22:22 onward is a single sustained male voice, consistent with Brian.

The object lesson is visual - the captions capture only the speaker's commentary ('Does the water look clear and pure?', 'Well, put some more in there'), so the exact mechanics of the demonstration are inferred.
The speaker names the church as 'Fellowship Bible Church' at 0:15:08, which is what the 'FBC' in this project refers to; no city is stated on the recording.

The sin/cross/forgiveness sequence and phrases like 'we fall short' and 'a new creation' are universal evangelical stock content and Scripture allusion, not evidence of dependence on any particular preacher.

This item should be dropped from the plagiarism comparison set rather than counted as a 'clean' sermon by the main preacher - including it would understate the dependence rate across the actual sermon corpus.
